clauses.title: Placement of Backfill
clauses.text: Backfill shall be placed to avoid damaging the foundation wall, the drainage tile, externally applied thermal insulation and waterproofing or dampproofing of the wall.

clauses.title: Grading of Backfill
clauses.text: Backfill shall be graded to prevent drainage towards the foundation after settling.

clauses.title: Deleterious Debris and Boulders
clauses.text: Backfill that is within 600 mm of the foundation shall be free of deleterious debris and boulders larger than 250 mm diam. (See Note A-9.12.3.3.(1).)

clauses.title: Deleterious Debris and Boulders
clauses.text: Except as provided in Sentence (3), backfill shall not contain pyritic material or material that is susceptible to ice lensing in concentrations that will damage the building to a degree that would adversely affect its stability or the performance of assemblies. (See Note A-9.4.4.4.(1).)

clauses.title: Deleterious Debris and Boulders
clauses.text: Backfill with material of any concentration that is susceptible to ice lensing is permitted where foundation walls are a) cast-in-place concrete, b) concrete block insulated on the exterior, or c) concrete block protected from the backfill by a material that serves as a slip plane. (See Note A-9.4.4.4.(1).)

clauses.title: Support of Footings
clauses.text: The soil in trenches beneath footings for sewers and watermains shall be compacted by tamping up to the level of the footing base, or shall be filled with concrete having a strength not less than 10 MPa to support the footing.

clauses.title: Scope and Application
clauses.text: This Section presents measures to control the ingress of water, moisture and soil gas.

clauses.title: Scope and Application
clauses.text: Subsection 9.13.2. applies to below-ground walls and floors-on-ground where drainage is provided in accordance with Section 9.14. over and along the entire below-ground portion of the foundation wall.

clauses.title: Scope and Application
clauses.text: Subsection 9.13.3. applies to below-ground walls, floors-on-ground and roofs of underground structures that are subject to hydrostatic pressure.

clauses.title: Scope and Application
clauses.text: Subsection 9.13.4. applies to walls, roofs and floors that are in contact with the ground.

clauses.title: Required Dampproofing
clauses.text: Except as provided in Article 9.13.3.1., where the exterior finished ground level is at a higher elevation than the ground level inside the foundation walls, exterior surfaces of foundation walls below ground level shall be dampproofed.

clauses.title: Required Dampproofing
clauses.text: Except as provided in Sentence (3) and Article 9.13.3.1., floors-on-ground shall be dampproofed.

clauses.title: Required Dampproofing
clauses.text: Dampproofing required in Sentence (2) need not be provided for a) floors in garages, b) floors in unenclosed portions of buildings, or c) floors installed over not less than 100 mm of coarse clean granular material containing not more than 10% of material that will pass a 4 mm sieve.

clauses.title: Dampproofing Materials
clauses.text: Materials installed to provide required dampproofing shall be a) capable of protecting assemblies against moisture transfer from the ground, b) compatible with adjoining materials, and c) resistant to mechanisms of deterioration that may reasonably be expected, given the nature, function and exposure of the materials.

clauses.title: Dampproofing Materials
clauses.text: Except as otherwise specified in this Section, materials used for exterior dampproofing shall a) conform to one of the following standards: i) ASTM D1227/D1227M, “Standard Specification for Emulsified Asphalt Used as a Protective Coating for Roofing,” Type III, Class I, ii) ASTM D4479/D4479M, “Standard Specification for Asphalt Roof Coatings – Asbestos-Free,” Type III, iii) CAN/CGSB-51.34, “Polyethylene sheet for use in building construction – Material specification,” or iv) CAN/CSA-A123.4, “Asphalt for Constructing Built-Up Roof Coverings and Waterproofing Systems,” or b) have a water vapour permeance of not more than 43 ng/(Pa×s×m2) when tested in accordance with Procedure B (wet cup) of ASTM E96/E96M, “Standard Test Methods for Gravimetric Determination of Water Vapor Transmission Rate of Materials,” and consist of one of the following material types: i) a vapour-resistant coating, ii) a cold-fluid-applied or hot-rubberized bituminous dampproofing membrane, iii) a liquid-applied or spray-applied asphalt-based emulsion dampproofing, or iv) a type III hot-applied asphalt.

clauses.title: Preparation of Surface
clauses.text: The area in which dampproofing is to be carried out shall be kept free of water during the application and curing of the dampproofing system.

clauses.title: Preparation of Surface
clauses.text: The surface to be dampproofed shall be prepared in accordance with the instructions of the dampproofing material manufacturer.

clauses.title: Preparation of Surface
clauses.text: Where the dampproofing material is to be applied on insulating concrete form (ICF) walls, the instructions of the ICF wall manufacturer shall be followed.

clauses.title: Preparation of Surface
clauses.text: Unit masonry walls to be dampproofed shall be parged on the exterior face below ground level with not less than 6 mm of mortar conforming to Section 9.20. coved over the footing.

clauses.title: Preparation of Surface
clauses.text: Concrete walls to be dampproofed shall have holes and recesses sealed with cement mortar or a mastic or sealant that is suitable for vertical applications and compatible with the dampproofing material.

clauses.title: Preparation of Surface
clauses.text: The surface required to be dampproofed shall be clean and dry and free of ice, snow, frost, dust, dirt, oil, grease, cracks, projections and depressions, loose particles and debris that could be detrimental to the performance of the material to be applied.

clauses.title: Application of Dampproofing Material
clauses.text: Exterior dampproofing shall be applied from finished ground level to the top of the exterior of the footing.

clauses.title: Application of Dampproofing Material
clauses.text: Unless otherwise stated in this Subsection, dampproofing shall be installed in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions with regard to a) surface priming, b) conditions during application, c) application quantity and rate, and d) curing times.

clauses.title: Application of Dampproofing Material
clauses.text: Joints, cracks and penetrations shall be sealed to maintain the continuity of the dampproofing, where the dampproofing material is not capable of bridging such discontinuities.

clauses.title: Moisture Protection for Interior Finishes
clauses.text: The interior surface of foundation walls below ground level shall be protected by means that minimize the ingress of moisture from the foundation wall into interior spaces, where a) a separate interior finish is applied to a concrete or unit masonry wall that is in contact with the soil, or b) wood members are placed in contact with such walls for the installation of insulation or finish.

clauses.title: Moisture Protection for Interior Finishes
clauses.text: Except as provided in Sentence (3), where the protection of interior finishes required in Sentence (1) consists of membranes or coatings, a) the membrane or coating shall extend from the basement floor surface up to the highest extent of the interior insulation or finish, but not higher than the exterior finished ground level, and b) no membrane or coating with a permeance less than 170 ng/(Pa×s×m2) shall be applied to the interior surface of the foundation wall above ground level between the insulation and the foundation wall.

clauses.title: Moisture Protection for Interior Finishes
clauses.text: Where insulation functions as both moisture protection for interior finishes and as a vapour barrier in accordance with Subsection 9.25.4., it shall be applied over the entire interior surface of the foundation wall.

clauses.title: Dampproofing of Floors-on-Ground
clauses.text: Where dampproofing is installed below the floor, it shall consist of a) polyethylene not less than 0.15 mm thick with joints lapped not less than 100 mm, b) type S roll roofing with joints lapped not less than 100 mm, or c) rigid extruded/expanded polystyrene with sealed or ship-lapped joints that has i) sufficient compressive strength to support the floor assembly, and ii) a water vapour permeance complying with Clause 9.13.2.2.(2)(b).

clauses.title: Dampproofing of Floors-on-Ground
clauses.text: Where dampproofing is installed between a floor-on-ground and a finished floor, it shall consist of a) rigid extruded/expanded polystyrene with sealed or ship-lapped joints that has i) sufficient compressive strength to support the floor assembly, and ii) a water vapour permeance complying with Clause 9.13.2.2.(2)(b), or b) polyethylene not less than 0.05 mm thick with joints lapped not less than 100 mm.

clauses.title: Required Waterproofing
clauses.text: Where hydrostatic pressure occurs, waterproofing is required for assemblies separating interior space from the ground to prevent the ingress of water into building assemblies and interior spaces.

clauses.title: Required Waterproofing
clauses.text: Waterproofing is required for roofs of underground structures to prevent the ingress of water into building assemblies and interior spaces.

clauses.title: Waterproofing Materials
clauses.text: Materials installed to provide required waterproofing shall be a) compatible with adjoining materials, and b) resistant to mechanisms of deterioration that may reasonably be expected, given the nature, function and exposure of the materials.

clauses.title: Waterproofing Materials
clauses.text: Materials used for exterior waterproofing shall conform to a) ASTM D1227/D1227M, “Standard Specification for Emulsified Asphalt Used as a Protective Coating for Roofing,” in which case, they shall be installed in accordance with Sentence 9.13.3.3.(3), b) ASTM D3019/D3019M, “Standard Specification for Lap Cement Used with Asphalt Roll Roofing, Non-Fibered, and Fibered,” where non-fibered and non-asbestos-fibered (Types I and III) asphalt roll roofing are permitted, c) ASTM D4479/D4479M, “Standard Specification for Asphalt Roof Coatings – Asbestos-Free,” in which case, they shall be installed in accordance with Sentence 9.13.3.3.(3) and with reinforcing material, d) ASTM D4637/D4637M, “Standard Specification for EPDM Sheet Used In Single-Ply Roof Membrane,” e) ASTM D4811/D4811M, “Standard Specification for Nonvulcanized (Uncured) Rubber Sheet Used as Roof Flashing,” f) ASTM D6878/D6878M, “Standard Specification for Thermoplastic Polyolefin Based Sheet Roofing,” g) CGSB 37-GP-9Ma, “Primer, Asphalt, Unfilled, for Asphalt Roofing, Dampproofing and Waterproofing,” where a primer is required, h) CAN/CGSB-37.50-M, “Hot-Applied, Rubberized Asphalt for Roofing and Waterproofing,” i) CAN/CGSB-37.54, “Polyvinyl Chloride Roofing and Waterproofing Membrane,” j) CGSB 37-GP-56M, “Membrane, Modified, Bituminous, Prefabricated, and Reinforced for Roofing,” k) CAN/CGSB-37.58-M, “Membrane, Elastomeric, Cold-Applied Liquid, for Non-Exposed Use in Roofing and Waterproofing,” l) CAN/CSA-A123.2, “Asphalt-Coated Roofing Sheets,” m) CAN/CSA-A123.4, “Asphalt for Constructing Built-Up Roof Coverings and Waterproofing Systems,” in which case, they shall be installed with reinforcing material, or n) CSA A123.17, “Asphalt Glass Felt Used in Roofing and Waterproofing.”

clauses.title: Preparation of Surface
clauses.text: Surfaces to be waterproofed shall be prepared in accordance with the instructions of the waterproofing material manufacturer.

clauses.title: Preparation of Surface
clauses.text: Where the waterproofing material is to be applied on ICF walls, the instructions of the ICF wall manufacturer shall be followed.

clauses.title: Preparation of Surface
clauses.text: Unit masonry walls that are to be waterproofed shall be parged on exterior surfaces below ground level with not less than 6 mm of mortar conforming to

clauses.title: Application of Waterproofing Membranes
clauses.text: Unless otherwise stated in this Subsection, waterproofing shall be installed in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions with regard to a) surface priming, b) conditions during application, c) the required number of layers of reinforcing fabric on foundation, footings, floors, walls and structural slabs, d) application quantity and rate, and e) curing times.

clauses.title: Application of Waterproofing Membranes
clauses.text: Waterproofing shall be continuous across joints and at junctions between different building elements.

clauses.title: Application of Waterproofing Membranes
clauses.text: The waterproofed surface shall be protected with a suitable material to minimize mechanical damage during backfilling.

clauses.title: Application of Waterproofing Membranes
clauses.text: The area in which the waterproofing is to be carried out shall be kept free of water during the application and curing of the waterproofing system.

clauses.title: Floor Waterproofing System
clauses.text: Basement floors-on-ground to be waterproofed shall have a system of membrane waterproofing provided between 2 layers of concrete, each of which shall be not less than 75 mm thick, with the floor membrane made continuous with the wall membrane to form a complete seal.

clauses.title: Application and Scope
clauses.text: This Subsection applies to a) wall, roof and floor assemblies separating conditioned space from the ground, and b) the rough-in to allow the future protection of conditioned space that is separated from the ground by a wall, roof or floor assembly.

clauses.title: Application and Scope
clauses.text: This Subsection addresses the leakage of soil gas from the ground into the building.

clauses.title: Protection from Soil Gas Ingress
clauses.text: All wall, roof and floor assemblies separating conditioned space from the ground shall be protected by an air barrier system conforming to Subsection 9.25.3.

clauses.title: Protection from Soil Gas Ingress
clauses.text: Unless the space between the air barrier system and the ground is designed to be accessible for the future installation of a subfloor depressurization system, dwelling units and buildings containing residential occupancies shall be provided with the rough-in for a radon extraction system conforming to Article 9.13.4.3.

clauses.title: Protection from Soil Gas Ingress
clauses.text: Where buildings are used for occupancies other than those described in Sentence (2), protection from radon ingress and the means to address high radon concentrations in the future shall conform to a) Article 9.13.4.3., or b) Parts 5 and 6 (see Article 5.4.1.1. and 6.2.1.1.). (See Note A-9.13.4.2.(3).)

clauses.title: Providing for the Rough-in for a Subfloor Depressurization System
clauses.text: Floors-on-ground shall be provided with a rough-in for subfloor depressurization consisting of a) a gas-permeable layer, an inlet and an outlet as described in Sentence (2), or b) clean granular material and a pipe as described in Sentence (3).

clauses.title: Providing for the Rough-in for a Subfloor Depressurization System
clauses.text: The rough-in referred to in Clause (1)(a) shall include a) a gas-permeable layer installed in the space between the air barrier and the ground to allow the depressurization of that space, b) an inlet that allows for the effective depressurization of the gas-permeable layer (see Note A-9.13.4.3.(2)(b) and (3)(b)(i)), and c) an outlet in the conditioned space that i) permits connection to depressurization equipment, ii) is sealed to maintain the integrity of the air barrier system, and iii) is clearly labeled to indicate that it is intended only for the removal of radon from below the floor-on-ground.

clauses.title: Providing for the Rough-in for a Subfloor Depressurization System
clauses.text: The rough-in referred to in Clause (1)(b) shall include a) clean granular material installed below the floor-on-ground in accordance with Sentence 9.16.2.1.(1), and b) a pipe not less than 100 mm in diameter installed through the floor, such that i) its bottom end opens into the granular layer required in Clause (a) at or near the centre of the floor and not less than 100 mm of granular material projects beyond the terminus of the pipe measured along its axis (see Note A-9.13.4.3.(2)(b) and (3)(b)(i)), ii) its top end permits connection to depressurization equipment and is provided with an airtight cap, and iii) the pipe is clearly labeled near the cap and, if applicable, every 1.8 m and at every change in direction to indicate that it is intended only for the removal of radon from below the floor-on-ground.

clauses.title: Application
clauses.text: This Section applies to subsurface drainage and to surface drainage.

clauses.title: Crawl Spaces
clauses.text: Drainage for crawl spaces shall conform to Section 9.18.

clauses.title: Floors-on-Ground
clauses.text: Drainage requirements beneath floors-on-ground shall conform to Section 9.16.

clauses.title: Foundation Wall Drainage
clauses.text: Unless it can be shown to be unnecessary, the bottom of every exterior foundation wall shall be drained by drainage tile or pipe laid around the exterior of the foundation in conformance with Subsection 9.14.3. or by a layer of gravel or crushed rock in conformance with Subsection 9.14.4.

clauses.title: Foundation Wall Drainage
clauses.text: Where mineral fibre insulation or crushed rock backfill is provided adjacent to the exterior surface of a foundation wall, a) the insulation or backfill shall extend to the footing level to facilitate the drainage of ground water to the foundation's drainage system (see Note A-9.14.2.1.(2)(a)), and b) any pyritic material in the crushed rock shall be limited to a concentration that will not damage the building to a degree that would adversely affect its stability or the performance of assemblies (see Sentence 9.12.3.3.(2) and Note A-9.4.4.4.(1)).

clauses.title: Material Standards
clauses.text: Drain tile and drain pipe for foundation drainage shall conform to a) ASTM C4, “Standard Specification for Clay Drain Tile and Perforated Clay Drain Tile,” b) ASTM C412M, “Standard Specification for Concrete Drain Tile,” c) ASTM C444M, “Standard Specification for Perforated Concrete Pipe,” d) ASTM C700, “Standard Specification for Vitrified Clay Pipe, Extra Strength, Standard Strength, and Perforated,” e) BNQ 3624-115, “Polyethylene (PE) Pipe and Fittings for Soil and Foundation Drainage,” f) CAN/CSA-B182.1, “Plastic drain and sewer pipe and pipe fittings,” or g) CAN/CSA-G401, “Corrugated steel pipe products.”

clauses.title: Minimum Size
clauses.text: Drain tile or pipe used for foundation drainage shall be not less than 100 mm in diam.

clauses.title: Installation
clauses.text: Drain tile or pipe shall be laid on undisturbed or well-compacted soil so that the top of the tile or pipe is below the bottom of the floor slab or the ground cover of the crawl space.

clauses.title: Installation
clauses.text: Drain tile or pipe with butt joints shall be laid with 6 mm to 10 mm open joints.

clauses.title: Installation
clauses.text: The top half of joints referred to in Sentence (2) shall be covered with sheathing paper, 0.10 mm polyethylene or No. 15 asphalt or tar-saturated felt.

clauses.title: Installation
clauses.text: The top and sides of drain pipe or tile shall be covered with not less than 150 mm of crushed stone or other coarse clean granular material containing not more than 10% of material that will pass a 4 mm sieve.

clauses.title: Type of Granular Material
clauses.text: Granular material used to drain the bottom of a foundation shall consist of a continuous layer of crushed stone or other coarse clean granular material containing a) not more than 10% of material that will pass a 4 mm sieve, and b) no pyritic material in a concentration that will damage the building to a degree that would adversely affect its stability or the performance of assemblies (see Note A-9.4.4.4.(1)).

clauses.title: Installation
clauses.text: Granular material described in Article 9.14.4.1. shall be laid on undisturbed or compacted soil to a minimum depth of not less than 125 mm beneath the footing of the building and extend not less than 300 mm beyond the outside edge of the footings.

clauses.title: Grading
clauses.text: The bottom of an excavation drained by a granular layer shall be graded so that the entire area described in Article 9.14.4.2. is drained to a sump conforming to Article 9.14.5.2.

clauses.title: Wet Site Conditions
clauses.text: Where because of wet site conditions soil becomes mixed with the granular drainage material, sufficient additional granular material shall be provided so that the top 125 mm are kept free of soil.

clauses.title: Drainage Disposal
clauses.text: Foundation drains shall drain to a sewer, drainage ditch or dry well.

clauses.title: Sump Pits
clauses.text: Where a sump pit is provided it shall be a) not less than 750 mm deep, b) not less than 0.25 m2 in area, and c) provided with a cover.

clauses.title: Sump Pits
clauses.text: Covers for sump pits shall be designed a) to resist removal by children, and b) to be airtight in accordance with Sentence 9.25.3.3.(7).

clauses.title: Sump Pits
clauses.text: Where gravity drainage is not practical, an automatic sump pump shall be provided to discharge the water from the sump pit described in Sentence (1) into a sewer, drainage ditch or dry well.

clauses.title: Dry Wells
clauses.text: Dry wells may be used only when located in areas where the natural groundwater level is below the bottom of the dry well.

clauses.title: Dry Wells
clauses.text: Dry wells shall be not less than 5 m from the building foundation and located so that drainage is away from the building.

clauses.title: Surface Drainage
clauses.text: The building shall be located or the building site graded so that water will not accumulate at or near the building.

clauses.title: Drainage away from Wells or Septic Disposal Beds
clauses.text: Surface drainage shall be directed away from the location of a water supply well or septic tank disposal bed.

clauses.title: Window Wells
clauses.text: Every window well shall be drained to the footing level or other suitable location.

clauses.title: Catch Basin
clauses.text: Where runoff water from a driveway is likely to accumulate or enter a garage, a catch basin shall be installed to provide adequate drainage.

clauses.title: Downspouts
clauses.text: Downspouts shall conform to Article 9.26.18.2.

clauses.title: General
clauses.text: Except as provided in Articles 9.15.1.2. and 9.15.1.3., this Section applies to a) concrete or unit masonry foundation walls and concrete footings not subject to surcharge i) on stable soils with an allowable bearing pressure of 75 kPa or greater, and ii) for buildings of wood-frame or masonry construction, b) wood-frame foundation walls and wood or concrete footings not subject to surcharge i) on stable soils with an allowable bearing pressure of 75 kPa or greater, and ii) for buildings of wood-frame construction, and c) flat insulating concrete form foundation walls and concrete footings not subject to surcharge (see Note A-9.15.1.1.(1)(c) and 9.20.1.1.(1)(b)) i) on stable soils with an allowable bearing pressure of 75 kPa or greater, and ii) for buildings of light-frame or flat insulating concrete form construction that are not more than 2 storeys in building height, with a maximum floor-to-floor height of 3 m.

clauses.title: General
clauses.text: Foundations for applications other than as described in Sentence (1) shall be designed in accordance with Section 9.4.

clauses.title: Permafrost
clauses.text: Buildings erected on permafrost shall have foundations designed by a designer competent in this field in accordance with the appropriate requirements of Part 4.

clauses.title: Foundations for Deformation-Resistant Buildings
clauses.text: Where the superstructure of a detached building conforms to the requirements of the deformation resistance test in CSA Z240.2.1, “Structural requirements for manufactured homes,” the foundation shall be constructed in conformance with a) the remainder of this Section, or b) CSA Z240.10.1, “Site preparation, foundation, and installation of buildings.”

clauses.title: Concrete
clauses.text: Concrete shall conform to Section 9.3.

clauses.title: Unit Masonry Construction
clauses.text: Concrete block shall conform to CSA A165.1, “Concrete block masonry units,” and shall have a compressive strength over the average net cross-sectional area of the block of not less than 15 MPa.

clauses.title: Unit Masonry Construction
clauses.text: Mortar, grout, mortar joints, corbelling and protection for unit masonry shall conform to Section 9.20.

clauses.title: Unit Masonry Construction
clauses.text: For concrete block foundation walls required to be reinforced, a) mortar shall be Type S, conforming to CAN/CSA-A179, “Mortar and Grout for Unit Masonry,” b) grout shall be coarse, conforming to CAN/CSA-A179, “Mortar and Grout for Unit Masonry,” and c) placement of grout shall conform to CAN/CSA-A371, “Masonry Construction for Buildings.”

clauses.title: Pier-Type Foundations
clauses.text: Where pier-type foundations are used, the piers shall be designed to support the applied loads from the superstructure.

clauses.title: Pier-Type Foundations
clauses.text: Where piers are used as a foundation system in a building of 1 storey in building height, the piers shall be installed to support the principal framing members and shall be spaced not more than 3.5 m apart along the framing, unless the piers and their footings are designed for larger spacings.

clauses.title: Pier-Type Foundations
clauses.text: The height of piers described in Sentence (2) shall not exceed 3 times their least dimension at the base of the pier.

clauses.title: Pier-Type Foundations
clauses.text: Where concrete block is used for piers described in Sentence (2), they shall be laid with cores placed vertically, and where the width of the building is 4.3 m or less, placed with their longest dimension at right angles to the longest dimension of the building.

clauses.title: Wood-Frame Foundations
clauses.text: Foundations of wood-frame construction shall conform to a) CSA S406, “Specification of permanent wood foundations for housing and small buildings,” or b) Part 4. (See Note A-9.15.2.4.(1).)

clauses.title: Footings Required
clauses.text: Footings shall be provided under walls, pilasters, columns, piers, fireplaces and chimneys that bear on soil or rock, except that footings may be omitted under piers or monolithic concrete walls if the safe loadbearing capacity of the soil or rock is not exceeded.

clauses.title: Support of Footings
clauses.text: Footings shall rest on undisturbed soil, rock or compacted granular fill.

clauses.title: Support of Footings
clauses.text: Granular fill shall not contain pyritic material in a concentration that will damage the building to a degree that would adversely affect its stability or the performance of assemblies. (See also Article 9.4.4.4. and Note A-9.4.4.4.(1).)

clauses.title: Application of Footing Width and Area Requirements
clauses.text: Except as provided in Sentence 9.15.3.4.(2), the minimum footing width or area requirements provided in Articles 9.15.3.4. to 9.15.3.7. shall apply to footings, where a) the footings support i) foundation walls of masonry, concrete, or flat insulating concrete form walls, ii) above-ground walls of masonry, flat insulating concrete form walls or light wood-frame construction, and iii) floors and roofs of light wood-frame construction, b) the span of supported joists does not exceed 4.9 m, and c) the specified live load on any floor supported by the footing does not exceed 2.4 kPa (see Table 4.1.5.3.).

clauses.title: Application of Footing Width and Area Requirements
clauses.text: Except as provided in Sentence 9.15.3.4.(2), where the span of the supported joists exceeds 4.9 m, footings shall be designed in accordance with Section 4.2.

clauses.title: Application of Footing Width and Area Requirements
clauses.text: Where the specified live load exceeds 2.4 kPa, footings shall be designed in accordance with Section 4.2.

clauses.title: Basic Footing Widths and Areas
clauses.text: Except as provided in Sentences (2) and (3) and in Articles 9.15.3.5. to 9.15.3.7., the minimum footing width or area shall comply with Table 9.15.3.4.

clauses.title: Basic Footing Widths and Areas
clauses.text: Where the supported joist span exceeds 4.9 m in buildings with light wood-frame walls, floors and roofs, strip footing widths shall be determined according to a) Section 4.2., or b) the following formula where W = minimum footing width, w = minimum width of footings supporting joists not exceeding 4.9 m, as defined by Table 9.15.3.4., Σ sjs = sum of the supported joist spans on each storey bearing on an exterior wall whose load is transferred to the footing, or sum of half of the supported joist spans on each storey bearing on both sides of an interior wall whose load is transferred to the footing, and storeys = number of storeys supported by the footing. (See Note A-9.15.3.4.(2).)

clauses.text: Where a foundation rests on gravel, sand or silt in which the water table level is less than the width of the footings below the bearing surface, a) the footing width for walls shall be not less than twice the width required by Sentences (1) and (2), and Articles 9.15.3.5. and 9.15.3.6., and b) the footing area for columns shall be not less than twice the area required by Sentences (1) and (2) and Article 9.15.3.7. clauses.title: Adjustments to Footing Widths for Exterior Walls
clauses.text: The strip footing widths for exterior walls shown in Table 9.15.3.4. shall be increased by a) 65 mm for each storey of masonry veneer over wood-frame construction supported by the foundation wall, b) 130 mm for each storey of masonry construction supported by the foundation wall, and c) 150 mm for each storey of flat insulating concrete form wall construction supported by the foundation wall.

clauses.title: Adjustments to Footing Widths for Interior Walls
clauses.text: The minimum strip footing widths for interior loadbearing masonry walls shown in Table 9.15.3.4. shall be increased by 100 mm for each storey of masonry construction supported by the footing.

clauses.title: Adjustments to Footing Widths for Interior Walls
clauses.text: Footings for interior non-loadbearing masonry walls shall be not less than 200 mm wide for walls up to 5.5 m high and the width shall be increased by 100 mm for each additional 2.7 m of height.

clauses.title: Adjustments to Footing Area for Columns
clauses.text: The footing area for column spacings other than shown in Table 9.15.3.4. shall be adjusted in proportion to the distance between columns.

clauses.title: Footing Thickness
clauses.text: Footing thickness shall be not less than the greater of a) 100 mm, or b) the width of the projection of the footing beyond the supported element.

clauses.title: Step Footings
clauses.text: Where step footings are used, a) the vertical rise between horizontal portions shall not exceed 600 mm, and b) the horizontal distance between risers shall not be less than 600 mm.

clauses.title: Flat Wall Insulating Concrete Form Units
clauses.text: Flat wall insulating concrete form units shall conform to CAN/ULC-S717.1, “Standard for Flat Wall Insulating Concrete Form (ICF) Units – Material Properties.”

clauses.title: Foundation Wall Thickness and Required Lateral Support
clauses.text: Except as required in Sentence (2), the thickness of foundation walls made of unreinforced concrete block, concrete core in flat wall insulating concrete forms or solid concrete and subject to lateral earth pressure shall conform to Table 9.15.4.2.-A for walls not exceeding 3.0 m in unsupported height.

clauses.title: Foundation Wall Thickness and Required Lateral Support
clauses.text: The concrete core in flat insulating concrete form foundation walls shall be not less than the greater of a) 150 mm, or b) the thickness of the concrete in the wall above. clauses.title: Foundation Wall Thickness and Required Lateral Support
clauses.text: The thickness and reinforcing of foundation walls made of reinforced concrete block and subject to lateral earth pressure shall conform to Table 9.15.4.2.-B and Sentences (4) to (7), where a) the walls are laterally supported at the top, b) average stable soils are encountered, and c) wind loads on the exposed portion of the foundation are no greater than 0.70 kPa.

clauses.title: Foundation Wall Thickness and Required Lateral Support
clauses.text: For concrete block walls required to be reinforced, continuous vertical reinforcement shall a) be provided at wall corners, wall ends, wall intersections, at changes in wall height, at the jambs of all openings and at movement joints, b) extend from the top of the footing to the top of the foundation wall, and c) where foundation walls are laterally supported at the top, have not less than 50 mm embedment into the footing, if the floor slab does not provide lateral support at the wall base.

clauses.title: Foundation Wall Thickness and Required Lateral Support
clauses.text: For concrete block walls required to be reinforced, a continuous horizontal bond beam containing not less than one 15M bar shall be installed a) along the top of the wall, b) at the sill and head of all openings greater than 1.20 m in width, and c) at structurally connected floors. clauses.title: Foundation Wall Thickness and Required Lateral Support
clauses.text: In concrete block walls required to be reinforced, all vertical bar reinforcement shall be installed along the centre line of the wall.

clauses.title: Foundation Wall Thickness and Required Lateral Support
clauses.text: In concrete block walls required to be reinforced, ladder- or truss-type lateral reinforcement not less than 3.8 mm in diameter (no. 9 ASWG) shall be installed in the bed joint of every second masonry course.

clauses.title: Foundation Walls Considered to be Laterally Supported at the Top
clauses.text: Sentences (2) to (4) pertain to lateral support for walls described in Sentence 9.15.4.2.(1).

clauses.title: Foundation Walls Considered to be Laterally Supported at the Top
clauses.text: Foundation walls shall be considered to be laterally supported at the top if a) such walls support a solid masonry superstructure or flat insulating concrete form wall, b) the floor joists are embedded in the top of the foundation walls, c) the floor system is anchored to the top of the foundation walls with anchor bolts, in which case the joists may run either parallel or perpendicular to the foundation walls, or d) they extend from the footing to no more than 300 mm above the finished ground level and are backfilled on both sides such that the difference in elevation between the finished ground levels on either side of the wall is no more than 150 mm.

clauses.title: Foundation Walls Considered to be Laterally Supported at the Top
clauses.text: Unless the wall around an opening is reinforced to withstand earth pressure, the portion of the foundation wall beneath an opening shall be considered laterally unsupported if a) the opening is more than 1.2 m wide, or b) the total width of the openings in the foundation wall constitutes more than 25% of the length of the wall.

clauses.title: Foundation Walls Considered to be Laterally Supported at the Top
clauses.text: For the purposes of Sentence (3), the combined width of the openings shall be considered as a single opening if the average width is greater than the width of solid wall between them.

clauses.title: Foundation Walls Considered to be Laterally Supported at the Top
clauses.text: Flat insulating concrete form foundation walls shall be considered to be laterally supported at the top if the floor joists are installed according to Article 9.20.17.5.

clauses.title: Foundation Walls Considered to be Laterally Supported at the Bottom
clauses.text: Flat insulating concrete form foundation walls shall be considered to be laterally supported at the bottom where the foundation wall a) supports backfill not more than 1.2 m in height, b) is supported at the footing by a shear key and at the top by the ground floor framing, or c) is doweled to the footing with not less than i) 15M bars spaced not more than 1.2 m o.c., or ii) 10M bars spaced not more than 600 mm o.c.

clauses.title: Reinforcement for Flat Insulating Concrete Form Foundation Walls
clauses.text: Horizontal reinforcement in flat insulating concrete form foundation walls shall a) consist of i) one 10M bar placed not more than 300 mm from the top of the wall, and ii) 10M bars at 600 mm o.c., and b) be located i) in the inside half of the wall section, and ii) with a minimum cover of 30 mm from the inside face of the concrete.

clauses.title: Reinforcement for Flat Insulating Concrete Form Foundation Walls
clauses.text: Vertical reinforcement in flat insulating concrete form foundation walls shall be a) provided in accordance with i) Table 9.15.4.5.-A for 150 mm walls, ii) Table 9.15.4.5.-B for 190 mm walls, and iii) Table 9.15.4.5.-C for 240 mm walls, b) located in the inside half of the wall section with a minimum cover of 30 mm from the inside face of the concrete wall, and c) where interrupted by wall openings, placed not more than 600 mm from each side of the openings.

clauses.title: Reinforcement for Flat Insulating Concrete Form Foundation Walls
clauses.text: Cold joints in flat insulating concrete form foundation walls shall be reinforced with no less than one 15M bar spaced at not more than 600 mm o.c. and embedded 300 mm on both sides of the joint.

clauses.title: Reinforcement for Flat Insulating Concrete Form Foundation Walls
clauses.text: Reinforcing around openings in flat insulating concrete form foundation walls shall comply with Article 9.20.17.3. or 9.20.17.4. clauses.title: Extension above Ground Level
clauses.text: Exterior foundation walls shall extend not less than 150 mm above finished ground level.

clauses.title: Reduction in Thickness
clauses.text: Where the top of a foundation wall is reduced in thickness to permit the installation of floor joists, the reduced section shall be not more than 350 mm high and not less than 90 mm thick.

clauses.title: Reduction in Thickness
clauses.text: Where the top of a foundation wall is reduced in thickness to permit the installation of a masonry exterior facing, the reduced section shall be a) not less than 90 mm thick, and b) tied to the facing material with metal ties conforming to Sentence 9.20.9.4.(3) spaced not more than i) 200 mm o.c. vertically, and ii) 900 mm o.c. horizontally.

clauses.title: Reduction in Thickness
clauses.text: The space between wall and facing described in Sentence (2) shall be filled with mortar.

clauses.title: Corbelling
clauses.text: Corbelling of masonry foundation walls supporting cavity walls shall conform to Article 9.20.12.2.

clauses.title: Crack Control Joints
clauses.text: Crack control joints shall be provided in foundation walls more than 25 m long at intervals of not more than 15 m.

clauses.title: Crack Control Joints
clauses.text: Joints required in Sentence (1) shall be designed to resist moisture penetration and shall be keyed to prevent relative displacement of the wall portions adjacent to the joint.

clauses.title: Interior Masonry Walls
clauses.text: Interior masonry foundation walls not subject to lateral earth pressure shall conform to Section 9.20.

clauses.title: Support of Floor Joists
clauses.text: Except as permitted in Sentence (2), foundation walls of hollow masonry units supporting floor joists shall be capped with a) not less than 50 mm of concrete, b) solid masonry units that are 100% solid and not less than 50 mm high, or c) semi-solid or hollow solid masonry units that have the top course completely filled with mortar, grout or concrete.

clauses.title: Support of Floor Joists
clauses.text: Capping required in Sentence (1) need not be provided a) in localities where termites are not known to occur, b) when the joists are supported on a wood plate not less than 38 mm by 89 mm, and c) when the siding overlaps the foundation wall not less than 12 mm.

clauses.title: Support of Beams
clauses.text: Not less than 190 mm depth of solid masonry shall be provided beneath beams supported on masonry.

clauses.title: Support of Beams
clauses.text: Where the beam referred to in Sentence (1) is supported below the top of the foundation walls, the ends of such beams shall be protected from the weather.

clauses.title: Pilasters
clauses.text: Pilasters shall be provided under beams that frame into unit masonry foundation walls 140 mm or less in thickness.

clauses.title: Pilasters
clauses.text: Pilasters required in Sentence (1) shall be not less than 90 mm by 290 mm and shall be bonded or tied into the wall.

clauses.title: Pilasters
clauses.text: The top 200 mm of pilasters required in Sentence (1) shall be solid masonry with the cells of hollow or semi-solid units filled with mortar, grout or concrete.

clauses.title: Foundation Walls below Ground
clauses.text: Concrete block foundation walls shall be parged on the exterior face below ground level as required in Section 9.13.

clauses.title: Foundation Walls above Ground
clauses.text: Exterior surfaces of concrete block foundation walls above ground level shall have tooled joints, or shall be parged or otherwise suitably finished.

clauses.title: Form Ties
clauses.text: All form ties shall be removed at least flush with the concrete surface.

clauses.title: Application
clauses.text: This Section applies to floors supported on ground or on granular fill that do not provide structural support for the superstructure.

clauses.title: Structural Floors
clauses.text: Floors-on-ground that support loads from the superstructure shall be designed in conformance with Part 4.

clauses.title: Required Floors-on-Ground
clauses.text: All spaces within dwelling units, except crawl spaces, shall be provided with a floor-on-ground, where a) access is provided to the space, and b) a floor supported by the structure is not provided.

clauses.title: Dampproofing and Waterproofing
clauses.text: Dampproofing and waterproofing shall conform to Section 9.13.

clauses.title: Required Installation of Granular Material
clauses.text: Except as provided in Sentence (2), not less than 100 mm of coarse clean granular material containing not more than 10% of material that will pass a 4 mm sieve shall be placed beneath floors-on-ground. (See also Subsection 9.13.4. and Note A-9.13.4.)

clauses.title: Required Installation of Granular Material
clauses.text: Granular material need not be installed under a) slabs in garages, carports or accessory buildings, or b) buildings of industrial occupancy where the nature of the process contained therein permits or requires the use of large openings in the building envelope even during the winter.

clauses.title: Support of Floors
clauses.text: Material that is susceptible to changes in volume due to variations in moisture content or chemical-microbiological oxidation shall not be used as fill beneath floors-on-ground in a concentration that will damage the building to a degree that would adversely affect its stability or the performance of assemblies. (See also Article 9.4.4.4. and Note A-9.4.4.4.(1).)

clauses.title: Support of Floors
clauses.text: Material that is susceptible to changes in volume due to freezing shall not be used as fill beneath floors-on-ground that will be subjected to freezing temperatures. (See also Article 9.4.4.4. and Note A-9.4.4.4.(1).)

clauses.title: Support of Floors
clauses.text: Except as provided in Sentence (4), fill beneath floors-on-ground shall be compacted.

clauses.title: Support of Floors
clauses.text: Fill beneath floors-on-ground need not be compacted where the material is clean coarse aggregate containing not more than 10% of material that will pass a 4 mm sieve.

clauses.title: Control of Water Ingress
clauses.text: Except as provided in Article 9.16.3.2. or where it can be shown to be unnecessary, ingress of water underneath a floor-on-ground shall be prevented by grading or drainage.

clauses.title: Hydrostatic Pressure
clauses.text: Where groundwater levels may cause hydrostatic pressure beneath a floor-on-ground, the floor-on-ground shall be a) a poured concrete slab, and b) designed to resist such pressures.

clauses.title: Floor Drains
clauses.text: When floor drains are required (see Section 9.31.), the floor surface shall be sloped so that no water can accumulate.

clauses.title: Surface Finish
clauses.text: The finished surface of concrete floor slabs shall be trowelled smooth and even.

clauses.title: Surface Finish
clauses.text: Dry cement shall not be added to the floor surfaces to absorb surplus water.

clauses.title: Topping Course
clauses.text: When a topping course is provided for a concrete floor slab, it shall consist of 1 part cement to 2.5 parts clean, well graded sand by volume, with a water/cement ratio approximately equal to that of the base slab.

clauses.title: Topping Course
clauses.text: When concrete topping is provided, it shall not be less than 20 mm thick.

clauses.title: Thickness
clauses.text: Concrete slabs shall not be less than 75 mm thick exclusive of concrete topping.

clauses.title: Bond Break
clauses.text: A bond-breaking material shall be placed between the slab and footings or rock.

clauses.title: Wood-Frame Floors
clauses.text: Floors-on-ground constructed of wood shall conform to CSA S406, “Specification of permanent wood foundations for housing and small buildings.”

clauses.title: Application
clauses.text: This Section applies to columns used to support a) beams carrying loads from not more than 2 wood-frame floors where i) the supported length of joists bearing on such beams does not exceed 5 m, and ii) the live load on any floor does not exceed 2.4 kPa (see Table 4.1.5.3.), b) beams or header joists carrying loads from not more than 2 levels of wood-frame balconies, decks or other accessible exterior platforms, or 1 level plus the roof, where i) the supported length of joists bearing on such beams or joists does not exceed 5 m, ii) the sum of the specified snow and occupancy loads does not exceed 4.8 kPa (see Sentence 9.4.2.3.(1) for the determination of load on platform-type constructions), and iii) the platform serves only a single suite of residential occupancy, or c) carport roofs (see Section 9.35.).

clauses.title: Application
clauses.text: Columns for applications other than as described in Sentence (1) shall be designed in accordance with Part 4.

clauses.title: Location
clauses.text: Columns shall be centrally located on a footing conforming to Section 9.15.

clauses.title: Lateral Support
clauses.text: Columns shall be securely fastened to the supported member to reduce the likelihood of lateral differential movement between the column and the supported member. (See also Article 9.23.6.2.)

clauses.title: Lateral Support
clauses.text: Except as permitted by Sentence (3), columns shall be laterally supported to resist racking a) directly, or b) by connection to the supported members. (See Note A-9.17.2.2.(2).)

clauses.title: Lateral Support
clauses.text: Columns need not be provided with lateral support as described in Sentence (2), where a) the distance from finished ground to the underside of the joists is not more than 600 mm, and b) the columns support a deck with no superstructure.

clauses.title: Size and Thickness
clauses.text: Except as permitted in Sentence (2), steel pipe columns shall have an outside diameter of not less than 73 mm and a wall thickness of not less than 4.76 mm.

clauses.title: Size and Thickness
clauses.text: Columns of sizes other than as specified in Sentence (1) are permitted to be used where the loadbearing capacities are shown to be adequate.

clauses.title: End Bearing Plates
clauses.text: Except as permitted in Sentence (2), steel columns shall be fitted with not less than 100 mm by 100 mm by 6.35 mm thick steel plates at each end, and where the column supports a wooden beam, the top plate shall extend across the full width of the beam.

clauses.title: End Bearing Plates
clauses.text: The top plate required in Sentence (1) need not be provided where a column supports a steel beam and provision is made for the attachment of the column to the beam.

clauses.title: Paint
clauses.text: Exterior steel columns shall be treated on the outside surface with at least one coat of rust-inhibitive paint.

clauses.title: Design of Steel Columns
clauses.text: Where the imposed load does not exceed 36 kN, adjustable steel columns shall conform to CAN/CGSB-7.2, “Adjustable Steel Columns.”

clauses.title: Design of Steel Columns
clauses.text: Steel columns other than those described in Sentence (1) shall be designed in accordance with Part 4.

clauses.title: Column Sizes
clauses.text: The width or diameter of a wood column shall be not less than the width of the supported member.

clauses.title: Column Sizes
clauses.text: Except as provided in Article 9.35.4.2., columns shall be not less than 184 mm for round columns and 140 mm by 140 mm for rectangular columns, unless calculations are provided to show that lesser sizes are adequate.

clauses.title: Materials
clauses.text: Wood columns shall be either solid, glued-laminated or built-up.

clauses.title: Materials
clauses.text: Built-up columns shall consist of not less than 38 mm thick full-length members a) bolted together with not less than 9.52 mm diam bolts spaced not more than 450 mm o.c., or b) nailed together with not less than 76 mm nails spaced not more than 300 mm o.c.

clauses.title: Materials
clauses.text: Glued-laminated columns shall conform to Section 4.3.

clauses.title: Columns in Contact with Concrete
clauses.text: Wood columns shall be separated from concrete in contact with the ground by 0.05 mm polyethylene film or Type S roll roofing.

clauses.title: Materials
clauses.text: Unit masonry columns shall be built of masonry units a) conforming to CSA A165.1, “Concrete block masonry units,” and b) having a compressive strength over the net area of the block of not less than 15 MPa.

clauses.title: Sizes
clauses.text: Unit masonry columns shall be not less than 290 mm by 290 mm or 240 mm by 380 mm in size.

clauses.title: Materials
clauses.text: Concrete shall conform to Section 9.3.

clauses.title: Sizes
clauses.text: Concrete columns shall be not less than 200 mm by 200 mm for rectangular columns and 230 mm diam for circular columns.

clauses.title: Application
clauses.text: This Section applies to crawl spaces whose exterior walls have less than 25% of their total area above exterior ground level open to the outdoors.

clauses.title: Foundations
clauses.text: Foundations enclosing crawl spaces shall conform to Section 9.15.

clauses.title: Heated and Unheated Crawl Spaces
clauses.text: Crawl spaces shall be considered to be heated where the space a) is used as a hot air plenum, b) contains heating ducts that are not sealed and insulated to minimize heat loss to the space, or c) is not separated from heated space in accordance with Section 9.25.

clauses.title: Heated and Unheated Crawl Spaces
clauses.text: Heating of heated crawl spaces shall conform to Section 9.33.

clauses.title: Heated and Unheated Crawl Spaces
clauses.text: Insulation, an air barrier system and a vapour barrier shall be installed in the walls of heated crawl spaces in accordance with Section 9.25.

clauses.title: Access Openings
clauses.text: An access opening of not less than 500 mm by 700 mm shall be provided to each crawl space where the crawl space serves a single dwelling unit, and not less than 550 mm by 900 mm for other crawl spaces.

clauses.title: Access Openings
clauses.text: Access openings shall be fitted with a door or hatch, except when the crawl space is heated and the access opening into the crawl space is from an adjacent heated space.

clauses.title: Ventilation of Unheated Crawl Spaces
clauses.text: Unheated crawl spaces shall be ventilated by natural or mechanical means.

clauses.title: Ventilation of Unheated Crawl Spaces
clauses.text: Where an unheated crawl space is ventilated by natural means, ventilation shall be provided to the outside air by not less than 0.1 m2 of unobstructed vent area for every 50 m2 of floor area.

clauses.title: Ventilation of Unheated Crawl Spaces
clauses.text: Vents shall be a) uniformly distributed on opposite sides of the building, and b) designed to prevent the entry of snow, rain and insects.

clauses.title: Ventilation of Heated Crawl Spaces
clauses.text: Heated crawl spaces shall be ventilated in accordance with Section 9.32.

clauses.title: Access Way to Services
clauses.text: Where equipment requiring service such as plumbing cleanouts, traps and burners is located in crawl spaces, an access way with a height and width of not less than 600 mm shall be provided from the access door to the equipment and for a distance of 900 mm on the side or sides of the equipment to be serviced.

clauses.title: Drainage
clauses.text: Except where it can be shown to be unnecessary, the ingress of water into a crawl space shall be controlled by grading or drainage.

clauses.title: Drainage
clauses.text: Drainage of foundation walls shall conform to Article 9.14.2.1.

clauses.title: Drainage
clauses.text: Drainage of the ground cover or floor-on-ground in the crawl space shall conform to Subsection 9.16.3.

clauses.title: Drainage
clauses.text: Drains shall conform to Section 9.14.

clauses.title: Ground Cover in Unheated Crawl Spaces
clauses.text: Where a crawl space is unheated, a ground cover shall be provided consisting of not less than a) 50 mm of asphalt, b) 100 mm of 15 MPa Portland cement concrete, c) Type S roll roofing, or d) 0.10 mm polyethylene.

clauses.title: Ground Cover in Unheated Crawl Spaces
clauses.text: Joints in sheet-type ground cover required in Sentence (1) shall be lapped not less than 100 mm and weighted down.

clauses.title: Ground Cover in Heated Crawl Spaces
clauses.text: Where a crawl space is heated, a ground cover consisting of not less than 0.15 mm polyethylene sheet conforming to CAN/CGSB-51.34, “Polyethylene sheet for use in building construction – Material specification,” shall be installed as part of an air barrier system in accordance with Subsection 9.25.3.

clauses.title: Ground Cover in Heated Crawl Spaces
clauses.text: The ground cover required in Sentence (1) shall have its joints lapped not less than 300 mm, and a) be sealed and evenly weighted down, or b) be covered with concrete not less than 50 mm thick.

clauses.title: Ground Cover in Heated Crawl Spaces
clauses.text: The perimeter of the ground cover required in Sentence (1) shall be sealed to the foundation wall. (See Notes A-9.13.4., A-9.25.3.4. and 9.25.3.6., and A-9.25.3.6.(2) and (3).)

clauses.title: Ground Cover in Heated Crawl Spaces
clauses.text: All penetrations of the ground cover required in Sentence (1) shall be sealed against air leakage. (See Subsection 9.25.3.)

clauses.title: Crawl Spaces as Warm Air Plenums
clauses.text: Only crawl spaces under 1-storey portions of dwelling units shall be used as warm-air plenums.

clauses.title: Crawl Spaces as Warm Air Plenums
clauses.text: Enclosing material in crawl spaces described in Sentence (1), including insulation, shall have a surface flame-spread rating not greater than 150.

clauses.title: Crawl Spaces as Warm Air Plenums
clauses.text: Combustible ground cover in crawl spaces described in Sentence (1) shall be protected beneath each register opening with noncombustible material.

clauses.title: Crawl Spaces as Warm Air Plenums
clauses.text: The noncombustible register protection described in Sentence (3) shall a) extend not less than 300 mm beyond the projection of the register opening, and b) have up-turned edges. (See Note A-9.18.7.1.(4).)

clauses.title: Required Venting
clauses.text: Except where it can be shown to be unnecessary, where insulation is installed between a ceiling and the underside of the roof sheathing, a space shall be provided between the insulation and the sheathing, and vents shall be installed to permit the transfer of moisture from the space to the exterior. (See Note A-9.19.1.1.(1).)

clauses.title: Vent Requirements
clauses.text: Except as provided in Sentence (2), the unobstructed vent area shall be not less than 1/300 of the insulated ceiling area.

clauses.title: Vent Requirements
clauses.text: Where the roof slope is less than 1 in 6 or in roofs that are constructed with roof joists, the unobstructed vent area shall be not less than 1/150 of the insulated ceiling area.

clauses.title: Vent Requirements
clauses.text: Required vents may be roof type, eave type, gable-end type or any combination thereof, and shall be distributed a) uniformly on opposite sides of the building, b) with not less than 25% of the required openings located at the top of the space, and c) with not less than 25% of the required openings located at the bottom of the space.

clauses.title: Vent Requirements
clauses.text: Except where each joist space is separately vented, roof joist spaces shall be interconnected by installing purlins not less than 38 mm by 38 mm on the top of the roof joists.

clauses.title: Vent Requirements
clauses.text: Vents shall comply with CAN3-A93-M, “Natural Airflow Ventilators for Buildings.”

clauses.title: Clearances
clauses.text: Except as provided in Sentence (2), not less than 63 mm of space shall be provided between the top of the insulation and the underside of the roof sheathing.

clauses.title: Clearances
clauses.text: At the junction of sloped roofs and exterior walls, where preformed baffles are used to contain the insulation, the baffles shall a) provide an unobstructed air space, between the insulation and the underside of the roof sheathing, that is i) not less than 25 mm in dimension, and ii) of sufficient cross area to meet the attic or roof space venting requirements of Article 9.19.1.2., and b) extend vertically not less than 50 mm above the top of the insulation.

clauses.title: Clearances
clauses.text: Ceiling insulation shall be installed in a manner that will not restrict the free flow of air through roof vents or through any portion of the attic or roof space.

clauses.title: Mansard or Gambrel Roof
clauses.text: The lower portion of a mansard or gambrel style roof need not be ventilated.

clauses.title: Mansard or Gambrel Roof
clauses.text: The upper portion of roofs described in Sentence (1) shall be ventilated in conformance with Articles 9.19.1.1. to 9.19.1.3.

clauses.title: Access
clauses.text: Every attic or roof space shall be provided with an access hatch where the open space in the attic or roof space measures a) 3 m2 or more in area, b) 1 m or more in length or width, and c) 600 mm or more in height over at least the area described in Clauses (a) and (b). (See Note A-9.19.2.1.(1).)

clauses.title: Access
clauses.text: The hatch required in Sentence (1) shall be not less than 550 mm by 900 mm except that, where the hatch serves not more than one dwelling unit, the hatch may be reduced to 0.32 m2 in area with no dimension less than 500 mm.

clauses.title: Access
clauses.text: Hatchways to attic or roof spaces shall be fitted with doors or covers.

clauses.title: General
clauses.text: Except as provided in Article 9.20.1.2., this Section applies to a) unreinforced masonry and masonry veneer walls not in contact with the ground, where i) the height of the walls constructed on the foundation walls does not exceed 11 m, and ii) the roof or floor assembly above the first storey is not of concrete construction, and b) flat insulating concrete form walls not in contact with the ground that (see Note A-9.15.1.1.(1)(c) and 9.20.1.1.(1)(b)) i) have a maximum floor-to-floor height of 3 m, ii) are erected in buildings not more than 2 storeys in building height, and iii) are erected in locations where the seismic spectral acceleration, Sa(0.2), is not greater than 0.4 (see Note A-9.20.1.2.).

clauses.title: General
clauses.text: For walls other than those described in Sentence (1), or where the masonry walls or insulating concrete form walls not in contact with the ground are designed for specified loads on the basis of ultimate and serviceability limit states, Subsection 4.3.2. shall apply.

clauses.title: Earthquake Reinforcement
clauses.text: In locations where the spectral acceleration, Sa(0.2), is greater than 0.55, loadbearing elements of masonry buildings more than 1 storey in building height shall be reinforced with not less than the minimum amount of reinforcement required by Subsection 9.20.15.

clauses.title: Earthquake Reinforcement
clauses.text: In locations where the spectral acceleration, Sa(0.2), is greater than 0.35 but less than or equal to 0.55, loadbearing elements of masonry buildings 3 storeys in building height shall be reinforced with not less than the minimum amount of reinforcement required by Subsection 9.20.15.

clauses.title: Masonry Unit Standards
clauses.text: Masonry units shall comply with a) ASTM C73, “Standard Specification for Calcium Silicate Brick (Sand-Lime Brick),” b) ASTM C126, “Ceramic Glazed Structural Clay Facing Tile, Facing Brick, and Solid Masonry Units,” c) ASTM C212, “Standard Specification for Structural Clay Facing Tile,” d) CAN/CSA-A82, “Fired masonry brick made from clay or shale,” e) CSA A165.1, “Concrete block masonry units,” f) CSA A165.2, “Concrete Brick Masonry Units,” or g) CSA A165.3, “Prefaced concrete masonry units.”

clauses.title: Used Brick
clauses.text: Used bricks shall be free of old mortar, soot or other surface coating and shall conform to Article 9.20.2.1.

clauses.title: Glass Blocks
clauses.text: Glass blocks shall not be used as loadbearing units or in the construction of fireplaces or chimneys.

clauses.title: Cellular Concrete
clauses.text: Masonry made with cellular concrete shall not be used in contact with the soil or exposed to the weather.

clauses.title: Stone
clauses.text: Stone shall be sound and durable.

clauses.title: Concrete Blocks Exposed to the Weather
clauses.text: Concrete blocks exposed to the weather shall have density and water absorption characteristics conforming to concrete types A, B, C, or D described in CSA A165.1, “Concrete block masonry units.”

clauses.title: Compressive Strength
clauses.text: The compressive strength of concrete blocks shall conform to Table 9.20.2.7. Table 9.20.2.7. clauses.title: Mortar Materials
clauses.text: Cementitious materials and aggregates for mortar and grout shall comply with CAN/CSA-A179, “Mortar and Grout for Unit Masonry.”

clauses.title: Mortar Materials
clauses.text: Water and aggregate shall be clean and free of significant amounts of deleterious materials.

clauses.title: Mortar Materials
clauses.text: Lime used in mortar shall be hydrated.

clauses.title: Mortar Materials
clauses.text: If lime putty is used in mortar, it shall be made by slaking quicklime in water for not less than 24 h or soaking hydrated lime in water for not less than 12 h.

clauses.title: Mortar and Grout Mixes
clauses.text: Mortar types shall be in accordance with Table 9.20.3.2.-A.

clauses.title: Mortar and Grout Mixes
clauses.text: Mortar for glass block masonry shall be a) Type S Portland cement-lime where exposed to the exterior, or b) Type S or N where protected from the exterior.

clauses.title: Mortar and Grout Mixes
clauses.text: Mortar shall be mixed within the proportion limits provided in Table 9.20.3.2.-B, with sufficient water to bring the mixture to a consistency adequate for laying masonry units.

clauses.title: Mortar and Grout Mixes
clauses.text: Grout shall be mixed within the proportion limits provided in Table 9.20.3.2.-C, with sufficient water to provide a suitable flow to fill all voids completely, without excessive segregation or bleeding.

clauses.title: Mortar and Grout Mixes
clauses.text: Except as provided in Sentence (6), mortar shall be used and placed in final position a) within 1.5 h after mixing when the air temperature is 25°C or higher, or b) within 2.5 h after mixing when the air temperature is less than 25°C.

clauses.title: Mortar and Grout Mixes
clauses.text: Mortar and grout containing a set-control admixture shall be manufactured off-site in a batching plant and shall be used and placed in final position within a time not exceeding the useful life stipulated by the manufacturer.

clauses.title: Mortar and Grout Mixes

clauses.title: Thickness
clauses.text: Except as provided in Sentence (2), mortar joint thickness for burned clay brick and concrete masonry units shall be 10 mm.

clauses.title: Thickness
clauses.text: Permitted tolerances in head and bed joints shall be not more than ± 5 mm.

clauses.title: Masonry Units
clauses.text: Hollow masonry units shall be laid with mortar applied to head and bed joints of both inner and outer face shells.

clauses.title: Masonry Units
clauses.text: Vertically aligned webs of hollow masonry units shall be laid in a full bed of mortar a) under the starting course, b) in all courses of columns, and c) where adjacent to cells or cavities that are to be filled with grout.

clauses.title: Masonry Units
clauses.text: Except for head joints left open for weep holes and ventilation, solid masonry units shall be laid with full head and bed joints.

clauses.title: Masonry Support
clauses.text: All masonry shall be supported on masonry, concrete or steel, except that masonry veneer walls may be supported on foundations of wood frame constructed in conformance with Sentence 9.15.2.4.(1). (See Note A-9.20.5.1.(1).)

clauses.title: Masonry Support
clauses.text: Every masonry wall shall be at least as thick as the wall it supports, except as otherwise permitted in Article 9.20.12.2.

clauses.title: Lintels or Arches
clauses.text: Masonry over openings shall be supported by steel, masonry or reinforced concrete lintels, or masonry arches.

clauses.title: Lintels or Arches
clauses.text: Steel angle lintels supporting masonry veneer above openings shall a) conform to Table 9.20.5.2., and b) have a bearing length not less than 90 mm. Table 9.20.5.2. clauses.title: Lintels or Arches
clauses.text: Steel angle lintels supporting masonry other than veneer, masonry and reinforced concrete lintels, and masonry arches shall be designed in accordance with Part 4 to support the imposed load.

tables.title: Maximum Allowable Spans for Steel Lintels Supporting Masonry Veneer

clauses.title: Lintels or Arches
clauses.text: Steel angle lintels supporting masonry shall be prime painted or otherwise protected from corrosion.

tables.title: Maximum Allowable Spans for Steel Lintels Supporting Masonry Veneer

clauses.title: Thickness of Exterior Walls
clauses.text: Masonry exterior walls, other than cavity walls, in 1-storey buildings and the top storeys of 2- and 3-storey buildings shall be not less than 140 mm thick, provided the walls are not more than 2.8 m high at the eaves and 4.6 m high at the peaks of gable ends.

clauses.title: Thickness of Exterior Walls
clauses.text: The exterior walls of the bottom storeys of 2-storey buildings, and exterior walls of the bottom 2 storeys of 3-storey buildings shall be not less than 190 mm thick.

clauses.title: Thickness of Exterior Walls
clauses.text: In exterior walls composed of more than one wythe, each wythe shall be not less than 90 mm thick.

clauses.title: Cavity Walls
clauses.text: Cavity walls shall be made with not less than 90 mm wide units if the joints are raked and not less than 75 mm wide units if the joints are not raked.

clauses.title: Cavity Walls
clauses.text: The width of a cavity in a cavity wall shall be not less than 50 mm and not greater than 150 mm.

clauses.title: Cavity Walls
clauses.text: The minimum thickness of cavity walls above the supporting base shall be 230 mm for the top 7.6 m and 330 mm for the remaining portion, except that where 75 mm wide units are used, the wall height above the top of the foundation wall shall not exceed 6 m.

clauses.title: Thickness of Interior Walls
clauses.text: The thickness of loadbearing interior walls shall be determined on the basis of the maximum lateral support spacing as provided in Sentences 9.20.10.1.(2) and (3).

clauses.title: Thickness of Interior Walls
clauses.text: The thickness of interior non-loadbearing walls shall be a) determined on the basis of the maximum lateral support spacing as provided in Sentences 9.20.10.1.(2) and (3), and b) in any case, not less than 65 mm.

clauses.title: Masonry Veneer
clauses.text: Except for masonry veneer where each masonry unit is supported individually by the structural backing, masonry veneer shall consist of solid masonry units not less than 75 mm thick.

clauses.title: Masonry Veneer
clauses.text: Veneer described in Sentence (1) over wood-frame walls shall have not less than a 25 mm air space behind the veneer.

clauses.title: Masonry Veneer
clauses.text: Masonry veneer less than 90 mm thick shall have unraked joints.

clauses.title: Masonry Veneer
clauses.text: Masonry veneer shall conform to Subsection 4.3.2., where the masonry units are required to be individually supported by the structural backing.

clauses.title: Parapet Walls
clauses.text: The height of parapet walls above the adjacent roof surface shall be not more than 3 times the parapet wall thickness.

clauses.title: Parapet Walls
clauses.text: Parapet walls shall be solid masonry a) with the cells of hollow or semi-solid units filled with mortar, grout, or concrete, and b) that extends from the top of the parapet to not less than 300 mm below the adjacent roof level.

clauses.title: Stone or Concrete Facings
clauses.text: Slab and panel facings of precast concrete and natural or artificial stone shall conform to Subsection 4.3.2.

clauses.title: Maximum Dimensions
clauses.text: Except as permitted in Sentence 9.20.7.2.(2) and Article 9.20.7.4., the depth of any chase or recess shall not exceed one third the thickness of the wall, and the width of the chase or recess shall not exceed 500 mm.

clauses.title: Minimum Wall Thickness
clauses.text: Except as permitted in Sentence (2) and Article 9.20.7.4., no chase or recess shall be constructed in any wall 190 mm or less in thickness.

clauses.title: Minimum Wall Thickness
clauses.text: Recesses may be constructed in 190 mm walls provided they do not exceed 100 mm in depth, 750 mm in height and 500 mm in width.

clauses.title: Separation of Chases or Recesses
clauses.text: Chases and recesses shall be not less than a) 4 times the wall thickness apart, and b) 600 mm away from any pilaster, cross wall, buttress or other vertical element providing required lateral support for the wall.

clauses.title: Non-Conforming Chases or Recesses
clauses.text: Chases or recesses that do not conform to the limits specified in Articles 9.20.7.1. to 9.20.7.3. shall be considered as openings, and any masonry supported above such a chase or recess shall be supported by a lintel or arch as provided in Article 9.20.5.2.

clauses.title: Chases or Recesses Cut into Walls
clauses.text: Chases and recesses shall not be cut into walls made with hollow units after the masonry units are in place.

clauses.title: Capping of Hollow Masonry Walls
clauses.text: Except as permitted in Sentence (2), loadbearing walls of hollow masonry units supporting roof or floor framing members shall be capped with not less than 50 mm of solid masonry or have the top course filled with concrete.

clauses.title: Capping of Hollow Masonry Walls
clauses.text: Capping required in Sentence (1) may be omitted where the roof framing is supported on a wood plate not less than 38 mm by 89 mm.

clauses.title: Cavity Walls Supporting Framing Members
clauses.text: Floor joists supported on cavity walls shall be supported on solid masonry units not less than 57 mm high.

clauses.title: Cavity Walls Supporting Framing Members
clauses.text: Floor joists described in Sentence (1) shall not project into the cavity.

clauses.title: Cavity Walls Supporting Framing Members
clauses.text: Roof and ceiling framing members bearing on cavity walls shall be supported on a) solid masonry units not less than 57 mm high that bridge the full thickness of the wall, or b) a wood plate not less than 38 mm thick, bearing not less than 50 mm on each wythe.

clauses.title: Bearing of Beams and Joists
clauses.text: The bearing area under beams and joists shall be sufficient to carry the supported load.

clauses.title: Bearing of Beams and Joists
clauses.text: In no case shall the minimum length of end bearing of beams supported on masonry be less than 90 mm.

clauses.title: Bearing of Beams and Joists
clauses.text: The length of end bearing of floor, roof or ceiling joists supported on masonry shall be not less than 40 mm.

clauses.title: Support of Beams and Columns
clauses.text: Beams and columns supported on masonry walls shall be supported on pilasters where the thickness of the masonry wall or wythe is less than 190 mm.

clauses.title: Support of Beams and Columns
clauses.text: Not less than 190 mm depth of solid masonry or concrete shall be provided under the beam or column referred to in Sentence (1).

clauses.title: Support of Beams and Columns
clauses.text: Pilasters required in Sentence (1) shall be bonded or tied to masonry walls.

clauses.title: Support of Beams and Columns
clauses.text: Concrete pilasters required in Sentence (1) shall be not less than 50 mm by 300 mm.

clauses.title: Support of Beams and Columns
clauses.text: Unit masonry pilasters required in Sentence (1) shall be not less than 100 mm by 290 mm.

clauses.title: Projection of Masonry Veneer Beyond Supporting Members
clauses.text: Masonry veneer of solid masonry units resting on a bearing support shall not project more than one third of the thickness of the veneer. (See Note A-9.20.8.5.(1).)

clauses.title: Projection of Masonry Veneer Beyond Supporting Members
clauses.text: Where the masonry veneer described in Sentence (1) is rough stone masonry, a) the projection shall be measured as the average projection of the units, and b) the thickness of the veneer shall be measured as the average thickness of the veneer.

clauses.title: Joints to be Offset or Reinforced
clauses.text: Vertical joints in adjacent masonry courses shall be offset unless each wythe of masonry is reinforced with the equivalent of not less than 2 corrosion-resistant steel bars of 3.76 mm diam placed in the horizontal joints at vertical intervals not exceeding 460 mm.

clauses.title: Joints to be Offset or Reinforced
clauses.text: Where joints in the reinforcing referred to in Sentence (1) occur, the bars shall be lapped not less than 150 mm.

clauses.title: Bonding or Tying of Other than Masonry Veneer
clauses.text: Except as provided in Article 9.20.9.5. regarding masonry veneer, masonry walls that consist of 2 or more wythes shall have the wythes bonded or tied together with masonry bonding units as described in Article 9.20.9.3. or with metal ties as described in Article 9.20.9.4.

clauses.title: Bonding
clauses.text: Where wythes are bonded together with masonry units, the bonding units shall comprise not less than 4% of the wall surface area.

clauses.title: Bonding
clauses.text: Bonding units described in Sentence (1) shall be spaced not more than 600 mm vertically and horizontally in the case of brick masonry and 900 mm o.c. in the case of block or tile.

clauses.title: Bonding
clauses.text: Units described in Sentence (1) shall extend not less than 90 mm into adjacent wythes.

clauses.title: Tying
clauses.text: Where 2 or more wythes are tied together with metal ties of the individual rod type, the ties shall conform to the requirements in Sentences (3) to (6).

clauses.title: Tying
clauses.text: Other ties may be used where it can be shown that such ties provide walls that are at least as strong and as durable as those made with the individual rod type.

clauses.title: Tying
clauses.text: Metal ties of the individual rod type shall a) be corrosion-resistant, b) have a minimum cross-sectional area of not less than 17.8 mm2, and c) have not less than a 50 mm portion bent at right angles at each end.

clauses.title: Tying
clauses.text: Metal ties of the individual rod type shall a) extend from within 25 mm of the outer face of the wall to within 25 mm of the inner face of the wall, b) be completely embedded in mortar except for the portion exposed in cavity walls, and c) be staggered from course to course.

clauses.title: Tying
clauses.text: Where 2 or more wythes in walls other than cavity walls and masonry veneer/masonry backing walls are tied together with metal ties of the individual rod type, the space between wythes shall be completely filled with mortar.

clauses.title: Tying
clauses.text: Ties described in Sentence (5) shall be a) located within 300 mm of openings and spaced not more than 900 mm apart around openings, and b) spaced not more than 900 mm apart horizontally and 460 mm apart vertically at other locations.

clauses.title: Tying
clauses.text: Except as required in Sentences (8) and (9), where the inner and outer wythes of cavity walls are tied with individual wire ties, the ties shall be spaced not more than 900 mm apart horizontally and 400 mm apart vertically.

clauses.title: Tying
clauses.text: Within 100 mm of the bottom of each floor or roof assembly where the cavity extends below the assemblies, the ties described in Sentence (7) shall be spaced not more than 600 mm apart horizontally.

clauses.title: Tying
clauses.text: Within 300 mm of any openings, the ties described in Sentence (7) shall be spaced not more than 900 mm apart.

clauses.title: Ties for Masonry Veneer
clauses.text: Masonry veneer 75 mm or more in thickness and resting on a bearing support shall be tied to masonry backing or to wood framing members with straps that are a) corrosion-resistant, b) not less than 0.76 mm thick, c) not less than 22 mm wide, d) shaped to provide a key with the mortar, e) pre-bent during manufacture to a right angle within 6 mm of the fastener hole, f) fastened with i) corrosion-resistant wood screws conforming to Sentence 9.23.3.1.(3) that have a minimum diameter of 4.16 mm (No. 8) and a wood penetration of not less than 38 mm, or ii) corrosion-resistant common spiral nails conforming to Sentence 9.23.3.1.(1) that are not less than 76 mm long and have a wood penetration of not less than 63 mm, and g) spaced in accordance with Table 9.20.9.5.
