clauses.title: Ties for Masonry Veneer
clauses.text: Where hot-dipped, zinc-coated straps are used to meet the requirements of Sentence (1), they shall be pre-bent and pre-drilled or pre-punched prior to hot-dip, zinc-coated galvanizing.

tables.title: Veneer Tie Spacing

clauses.title: Ties for Masonry Veneer
clauses.text: Masonry veneer individually supported by masonry or wood-frame backing shall be secured to the backing in conformance with Subsection 4.3.2.

tables.title: Veneer Tie Spacing

clauses.title: Reinforcing for Glass Block
clauses.text: Glass block shall have horizontal joint reinforcement of 2 corrosion-resistant bars of not less than 3.76 mm diam or expanded metal strips not less than 75 mm wide a) spaced at vertical intervals of not more than 600 mm for units 200 mm or less in height, and b) installed in every horizontal joint for units higher than 200 mm.

clauses.title: Reinforcing for Glass Block
clauses.text: Reinforcement required in Sentence (1) shall be lapped not less than 150 mm.

clauses.title: Lateral Support Required
clauses.text: Masonry walls shall be laterally supported by floor or roof construction or by intersecting masonry walls or buttresses.

clauses.title: Lateral Support Required
clauses.text: The spacing of supports required in Sentence (1) shall be not more than a) 20 times the wall thickness for all loadbearing walls and exterior non-loadbearing walls, and b) 36 times the wall thickness for interior non-loadbearing walls.

clauses.title: Lateral Support Required
clauses.text: In applying Sentence (2), the thickness of cavity walls shall be taken as the greater of a) two-thirds of the sum of the thicknesses of the wythes, or b) the thickness of the thicker wythe.

clauses.title: Lateral Support Required
clauses.text: Floor and roof constructions providing lateral support for walls as required in Sentence (1) shall be constructed to transfer lateral loads to walls or buttresses approximately at right angles to the laterally supported walls.

clauses.title: Anchorage to Floor or Roof Assemblies where Masonry Walls Require
clauses.text: Where required to receive lateral support (see Subsection 9.20.10.), masonry walls shall be anchored to each floor or roof assembly at maximum intervals of 2 m, except that anchorage to floor joists not more than 1 m above grade may be omitted.

clauses.title: Anchorage to Floor or Roof Assemblies where Masonry Walls Require
clauses.text: Anchors required in Sentence (1) shall be corrosion-resistant and be not less than the equivalent of 40 mm by 4.76 mm thick steel straps.

clauses.title: Anchorage to Floor or Roof Assemblies where Masonry Walls Require
clauses.text: Anchors required in Sentence (1) shall be shaped to provide a mechanical key with the masonry and shall be securely fastened to the horizontal support to develop the full strength of the anchor.

clauses.title: Anchorage to Floor or Roof Assemblies where Masonry Walls Require
clauses.text: When joists are parallel to the wall, anchors required in Sentence (1) shall extend across not less than 3 joists.

clauses.title: Bonding and Tying Intersecting Masonry Walls where Walls Require
clauses.text: Where required to provide lateral support, intersecting walls shall be bonded or tied together.

clauses.title: Bonding and Tying Intersecting Masonry Walls where Walls Require
clauses.text: Where bonding is used to satisfy the requirements of Sentence (1), 50% of the adjacent masonry units in the intersecting wall, distributed uniformly over the height of the intersection, shall be embedded in the laterally supported wall.

clauses.title: Bonding and Tying Intersecting Masonry Walls where Walls Require
clauses.text: Where tying is used to satisfy the requirements of Sentence (1), the ties shall be a) corrosion-resistant metal, b) equivalent to not less than 4.76 mm by 40 mm steel strapping, c) spaced not more than 800 mm o.c. vertically, and d) shaped at both ends to provide sufficient mechanical key to develop the strength of the ties.

clauses.title: Anchoring Intersecting Wood-Frame Walls to Masonry Walls
clauses.text: Wood-frame walls shall be anchored to masonry walls that they intersect with not less than 4.76 mm diam corrosion-resistant steel rods spaced not more than 900 mm o.c. vertically.

clauses.title: Anchoring Intersecting Wood-Frame Walls to Masonry Walls
clauses.text: Anchors required in Sentence (1) shall be fastened to the wood framing at one end and shaped to provide a mechanical key at the other end to develop the strength of the anchor.

clauses.title: Anchoring Wood-Frame Roof Systems to Masonry Walls
clauses.text: Except as permitted in Sentence (2), roof systems of wood-frame construction shall be anchored to exterior masonry walls by not less than 12.7 mm diam anchor bolts, a) spaced not more than 2.4 m apart, b) embedded not less than 90 mm into the masonry, and c) fastened to a rafter plate of not less than 38 mm thick lumber.

clauses.title: Anchoring Wood-Frame Roof Systems to Masonry Walls
clauses.text: The roof system described in Sentence (1) is permitted to be anchored by nailing the wall furring strips to the side of the rafter plate.

clauses.title: Anchoring Masonry Cornices, Sills and Trim to Masonry Walls
clauses.text: Cornices, sills or other trim of masonry material which project beyond the wall face shall have not less than 65% of their mass, but not less than 90 mm, within the wall or shall be adequately anchored to the wall with corrosion-resistant anchors.

clauses.title: Anchoring to Masonry Piers
clauses.text: Where anchor bolts are to be placed in the top of a masonry pier, the pier shall conform to the requirements of Sentence 9.15.2.3.(4) and shall be capped with concrete or reinforced masonry not less than 200 mm thick.

clauses.title: Corbelling
clauses.text: All corbelling shall consist of solid masonry units.

clauses.title: Corbelling
clauses.text: The units referred to in Sentence (1) shall be corbelled so that the horizontal projection of any unit does not exceed 25 mm and the total projection does not exceed one third of the total wall thickness.

clauses.title: Corbelling for Cavity Walls
clauses.text: Cavity walls of greater thickness than the foundation wall on which they rest shall not be corbelled but may project 25 mm over the outer face of the foundation wall disregarding parging.

clauses.title: Corbelling for Cavity Walls
clauses.text: Where the foundation wall referred to in Sentence (1) is unit masonry, it is permitted to be corbelled to meet flush with the inner face of a cavity wall provided a) the projection of each course does not exceed half the height or one third the thickness of the corbelled unit, and b) the total corbel does not exceed one third of the foundation wall thickness. (See Note A-9.20.12.2.(2).)

clauses.title: Corbelling for Masonry Veneer
clauses.text: Masonry veneer resting on a bearing support shall not project more than 25 mm beyond the supporting base where the veneer is not less than 90 mm thick, and 12 mm beyond the supporting base where the veneer is less than 90 mm thick.

clauses.title: Corbelling for Masonry Veneer
clauses.text: In the case of rough stone veneer, the projection, measured as the average projection of the stone units, shall not exceed one-third the bed width beyond the supporting base.

clauses.title: Materials for Flashing
clauses.text: Materials used for flashing shall conform to Table 9.20.13.1. Table 9.20.13.1. clauses.title: Materials for Flashing
clauses.text: Aluminum flashing in contact with masonry or concrete shall be effectively coated or separated from the masonry or concrete by an impervious membrane.

clauses.title: Fastening of Flashing
clauses.text: Fastening devices for flashing shall be corrosion-resistant and, where metal flashing is used, shall be compatible with the flashing with respect to galvanic action.

clauses.title: Location of Flashing
clauses.text: Flashing shall be installed in masonry and masonry veneer walls a) beneath jointed masonry window sills, b) over the back and top of parapet walls, c) over the heads of glass block panels, d) beneath weep holes, and e) over the heads of window or door openings in exterior walls when the vertical distance between the top of a window or door frame and the bottom edge of the eave exceeds one-quarter of the horizontal eave overhang.

clauses.title: Extension of Flashing
clauses.text: When installed beneath jointed masonry window sills or over the heads of openings, flashing shall extend from the front edge of the masonry up behind the sill or lintel.

clauses.title: Flashing for Weep Holes in Masonry/Masonry Walls
clauses.text: Flashing beneath weep holes in cavity walls and masonry veneer/masonry backing walls shall a) be bedded not less than 25 mm in the inside wythe, b) extend to not less than 5 mm beyond the outer face of the building element below the flashing, and c) be installed with a nominally horizontal slope toward the outside wythe.

clauses.title: Flashing for Weep Holes in Masonry Veneer
clauses.text: Flashing beneath weep holes in masonry veneer over masonry backing walls shall conform to the flashing requirements for cavity walls and masonry veneer/masonry backing walls in Article 9.20.13.5.

clauses.title: Flashing for Weep Holes in Masonry Veneer
clauses.text: Flashing beneath weep holes in masonry veneer over wood-frame walls shall be installed so that it extends from a point not less than 5 mm beyond the outer face of the building element below the flashing to a point 150 mm up the wood-frame wall.

clauses.title: Flashing for Weep Holes in Masonry Veneer
clauses.text: Where the frame wall is sheathed with a sheathing membrane, a non-wood-based rigid exterior insulating sheathing or a semi-rigid insulating sheathing with an integral sheathing membrane, the flashing shall be installed behind the sheathing membrane or insulating sheathing.

clauses.title: Flashing for Weep Holes in Masonry Veneer
clauses.text: Flashing described in Sentence (2) is permitted to conform to the requirements for concealed flashing in Table 9.20.13.1.

clauses.title: Flashing Joints
clauses.text: Joints in flashing shall be made watertight.

clauses.title: Required Weep Holes
clauses.text: Weep holes spaced not more than 800 mm apart shall be provided at the bottom of a) cavities in cavity walls, and b) cavities or air spaces in masonry veneer walls.

clauses.title: Required Weep Holes
clauses.text: The cavities or air spaces described in Sentence (1) shall include those above lintels over window and door openings required to be flashed in conformance with Article 9.20.13.3.

clauses.title: Protection of Interior Finish
clauses.text: Except as provided in Sentence (3), where the interior finish of the exterior walls of a building is a type that may be damaged by moisture, exterior masonry walls, other than cavity walls or walls that are protected for their full height by a roof of a carport or porch, shall be covered on the interior surface with sheathing membrane conforming to CAN/CGSB-51.32-M, “Sheathing, Membrane, Breather Type,” lapped not less than 100 mm at the joints.

clauses.title: Protection of Interior Finish
clauses.text: In situations described in Sentence (1), flashing shall be provided where water will accumulate, to lead it to the exterior.

clauses.title: Protection of Interior Finish
clauses.text: Where insulation that effectively limits the passage of water is applied by a waterproof adhesive or mortar directly to parged masonry, the requirements for sheathing membrane in Sentence (1) do not apply. (See Note A-9.20.13.9.(3).)

clauses.title: Mortar Droppings
clauses.text: Cavity walls shall be constructed so that mortar droppings are prevented from forming a bridge to allow the passage of rain water across the cavity.

clauses.title: Caulking at Door and Window Frames
clauses.text: The junction of door and window frames with masonry shall be caulked in conformance with Subsection 9.27.4.

clauses.title: Drips beneath Window Sills
clauses.text: Where no flashing is installed beneath window sills, such sills shall be provided with a drip not less than 25 mm from the wall surface.

clauses.title: Laying Temperature of Mortar and Masonry
clauses.text: Mortar and masonry shall be maintained at a temperature not below 5°C during installation and for not less than 48 h after installation.

clauses.title: Laying Temperature of Mortar and Masonry
clauses.text: No frozen material shall be used in mortar mix.

clauses.title: Protection from Weather
clauses.text: The top surface of uncompleted masonry exposed to the weather shall be completely covered with a waterproofing material when construction is not in progress.

clauses.title: Amount of Reinforcement
clauses.text: Where reinforcement is required in this Section, masonry walls shall be reinforced horizontally and vertically with steel having a total cross-sectional area of not less than 0.002 times the horizontal cross-sectional area of the wall, so that not less than one-third of the required steel area is installed either horizontally or vertically and the remainder in the other direction.

clauses.title: Installation Standard
clauses.text: Where reinforcement for masonry is required in this Section, it shall be installed in conformance with the requirements for reinforced masonry as contained in CAN/CSA-A371, “Masonry Construction for Buildings.”

clauses.title: Corrosion Resistance of Connectors
clauses.text: Carbon steel connectors required to be corrosion-resistant shall be galvanized to at least the minimum standards in Table 9.20.16.1. Table 9.20.16.1. clauses.title: Thickness of Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls
clauses.text: The thickness of the concrete in flat insulating concrete form walls not in contact with the ground shall be a) not less than 140 mm, and b) constant for the entire height of the wall.

clauses.title: Reinforcement for Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls
clauses.text: Horizontal reinforcement in above-grade flat insulating concrete form walls shall a) consist of i) one 10M bar placed not more than 300 mm from the top of the wall, and ii) 10M bars at 600 mm o.c., and b) be placed in the middle third of the wall section.

clauses.title: Reinforcement for Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls
clauses.text: Vertical reinforcement in above-grade flat insulating concrete form walls shall a) consist of 10M bars at 400 mm o.c., and b) be placed in the middle third of the wall section.

clauses.title: Reinforcement for Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls
clauses.text: Vertical reinforcement required by Sentence (2) and interrupted by wall openings shall be placed not more than 600 mm from each side of the opening.

clauses.title: Openings in Non-Loadbearing Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls
clauses.text: No openings shall occur within 1 200 mm of interior and exterior corners of exterior non-loadbearing flat insulating concrete form walls.

clauses.title: Openings in Non-Loadbearing Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls
clauses.text: Portions of walls above openings in non-loadbearing flat insulating concrete form walls shall have a minimum depth of concrete of no less than 200 mm across the width of the opening.

clauses.title: Openings in Non-Loadbearing Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls
clauses.text: Openings that are more than 600 mm but not more than 3 000 mm in width in non-loadbearing flat insulating concrete form walls shall be reinforced at the top and bottom with one 10M bar.

clauses.title: Openings in Non-Loadbearing Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls
clauses.text: Openings more than 3 000 mm in width in non-loadbearing flat insulating concrete form walls shall be reinforced on all four sides with two 10M bars.

clauses.title: Openings in Non-Loadbearing Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls
clauses.text: Reinforcing bars described in Sentences (3) and (4) shall extend 600 mm beyond the edges of the opening.

clauses.title: Openings in Non-Loadbearing Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls
clauses.text: The cumulative width of openings in non-loadbearing flat insulating concrete form walls shall not make up more than 70% of the length of any wall.

clauses.title: Openings in Loadbearing Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls
clauses.text: No openings shall occur within 1 200 mm of interior and exterior corners of exterior loadbearing flat insulating concrete form walls.

clauses.title: Openings in Loadbearing Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls
clauses.text: In loadbearing flat insulating concrete form walls, lintels shall be provided over all openings wider than 900 mm.

clauses.title: Openings in Loadbearing Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls
clauses.text: Lintels described in Sentence (2) shall be constructed in accordance with Span Table 9.20.17.4.-A, 9.20.17.4.-B or 9.20.17.4.-C.

clauses.title: Openings in Loadbearing Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls
clauses.text: Lintels described in Sentence (2) over openings wider than 1 200 mm shall be reinforced for shear with 10M stirrups at a maximum spacing of half the distance from the bottom reinforcing bar to the top of the lintel.

clauses.title: Framing Supported on Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls
clauses.text: Floor joists supported on the side of flat insulating concrete form walls shall be supported with joist hangers secured to wood ledger boards.

clauses.title: Framing Supported on Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls
clauses.text: The ledger boards referred to in Sentence (1) shall be not less than a) 38 mm thick, and b) the depth of the floor joists.

clauses.title: Framing Supported on Flat Insulating Concrete Form Walls
clauses.text: Anchor bolts shall be used to secure ledger boards to flat insulating concrete form walls and shall be a) embedded in the wall to a depth not less than 100 mm, and b) spaced in accordance with Table 9.20.17.5.

clauses.text: Floor joists and building frames supported on the top of flat insulating concrete form walls shall be anchored in conformance with Article 9.23.6.1. Table 9.20.17.5. clauses.title: Anchoring of Roof Framing to the Top of Flat Insulating Concrete
clauses.text: Roof framing supported on the top of flat insulating concrete form walls shall be fixed to the top plates, which shall be anchored to the wall with anchor bolts a) not less than 12.7 mm in diameter, and b) spaced at not more than 1 200 mm o.c.

clauses.title: Anchoring of Roof Framing to the Top of Flat Insulating Concrete
clauses.text: The anchor bolts described in Sentence (1) shall be placed in the centre of the flat insulating concrete form wall and shall be embedded no less than 100 mm into the concrete.

clauses.title: Anchoring of Roof Framing to the Top of Flat Insulating Concrete
clauses.text: Attachment of roof framing to wood top plates shall be in accordance with Table 9.23.3.4.

clauses.title: Protection from Precipitation and Damage
clauses.text: Above-ground flat insulating concrete form walls shall be protected from precipitation and damage in conformance with Section 9.27.

clauses.title: Application
clauses.text: This Section applies to a) rectangular masonry or concrete chimneys not more than 12 m in height serving fireplaces or serving appliances having a combined total rated heat output of 120 kW or less, and b) flue pipes connected to such chimneys.

clauses.title: Application
clauses.text: Chimneys, other than those described in Sentence (1), gas vents and flue pipes serving gas-, oil- or solid-fuel-burning appliances and their associated equipment, including stoves, cooktops, ovens and space heaters, covered by the standards referenced in Sentences 9.33.5.2.(1) and 9.33.5.3.(1) shall conform to Subsection 9.33.10.

clauses.title: Application
clauses.text: Chimneys and flue pipes other than those described in Sentences (1) and (2) shall conform to Section 6.3.

clauses.title: Chimney or Flue Pipe Walls
clauses.text: The walls of any chimney or flue pipe shall be constructed so as to be smoke- and flame-tight.

clauses.title: Chimney Flue Limitations
clauses.text: A chimney flue that serves a fireplace or incinerator shall not serve any other appliance.

clauses.title: Chimney Flue Limitations
clauses.text: A chimney flue that serves a solid-fuel-burning appliance shall not be connected to a natural-gas- or propane-fired appliance.

clauses.title: Chimney Flue Limitations
clauses.text: A chimney flue that serves a solid-fuel-burning appliance shall not be connected to an oil-burning appliance unless the solid-fuel-burning appliance is certified for such installation and the installation of both appliances meets the requirements of the relevant standards referenced in Article 9.33.5.2.

clauses.title: Connections of More Than One Appliance
clauses.text: Except as required by Article 9.21.2.1., where two or more fuel-burning appliances are connected to the same chimney flue, the connections shall be made as described in Sentences (2) to (4) and an adequate draft shall be provided for the connected appliances in conformance with the requirements of the relevant standards listed in Subsection 9.33.10.

clauses.title: Connections of More Than One Appliance
clauses.text: Where 2 or more fuel-burning appliances are connected to the same chimney flue, the appliances shall be located on the same storey.

clauses.title: Connections of More Than One Appliance
clauses.text: The connection referred to in Sentence (2) for a solid-fuel-burning appliance shall be made below connections for appliances burning other fuels.

clauses.title: Connections of More Than One Appliance
clauses.text: The connection referred to in Sentence (2) for a liquid-fuel-burning appliance shall be made below any connections for appliances burning natural gas or propane.

clauses.title: Inclined Chimney Flues
clauses.text: Chimney flues shall not be inclined more than 45° to the vertical.

clauses.title: Size of Chimney Flues
clauses.text: Except for chimneys serving fireplaces, the size of a chimney flue shall conform to the requirements of the appliance installation standards referenced in Sentences 9.33.5.2.(1) and 9.33.5.3.(1).

clauses.title: Size of Chimney Flues
clauses.text: Where a chimney flue serves only one appliance, the flue area shall be at least equal to that of the flue pipe connected to it.

clauses.title: Oval Chimney Flues
clauses.text: The width of an oval chimney flue shall be not less than two-thirds its breadth.

clauses.title: Lining Materials
clauses.text: Every masonry or concrete chimney shall have a lining of clay, concrete, firebrick or metal.

clauses.title: Joints in Chimney Liners
clauses.text: Joints of chimney liners shall be sealed to provide a barrier to the passage of flue gases and condensate into the cavity between the liner and the surrounding masonry.

clauses.title: Joints in Chimney Liners
clauses.text: Joints of clay, concrete or firebrick chimney liners shall be struck flush to provide a straight, smooth, aligned chimney flue.

clauses.title: Clay Liners
clauses.text: Clay liners shall conform to CAN/CSA-A324-M, “Clay Flue Liners.”

clauses.title: Clay Liners
clauses.text: Liners referred to in Sentence (1) shall be not less than 15.9 mm thick and shall be capable of resisting, without softening or cracking, a temperature of 1 100°C.

clauses.title: Firebrick Liners
clauses.text: Firebrick liners shall conform to ASTM C27, “Standard Classification of Fireclay and High-Alumina Refractory Brick.”

clauses.title: Firebrick Liners
clauses.text: Firebrick liners shall be laid with high temperature cement mortar conforming to CAN/CGSB-10.3, “Air Setting Refractory Mortar.”

clauses.title: Concrete Liners
clauses.text: Concrete flue liners shall conform to Clause 4.2.6.4 of CAN/CSA-A405-M, “Design and Construction of Masonry Chimneys and Fireplaces.”

clauses.title: Metal Liners
clauses.text: Metal liners shall be constructed of not less than 0.3 mm thick stainless steel.

clauses.title: Metal Liners
clauses.text: Metal liners referred to in Sentence (1) shall only be used in chimneys serving gas- or oil-burning appliances. (See Note A-9.21.3.6.(2).)

clauses.title: Installation of Chimney Liners
clauses.text: Chimney liners shall be installed when the surrounding masonry or concrete is placed.

clauses.title: Spaces between Liners and Surrounding Masonry
clauses.text: A space not less than 10 mm wide shall be left between a chimney liner and surrounding masonry.

clauses.title: Spaces between Liners and Surrounding Masonry
clauses.text: The space required in Sentence (1) shall not be filled with mortar.

clauses.title: Mortar for Chimney Liners
clauses.text: Chimney liners used in chimneys for solid-fuel-burning appliances shall be laid in a full bed of a) high temperature cement mortar conforming to CAN/CGSB-10.3, “Air Setting Refractory Mortar,” or b) mortar consisting of 1 part Portland cement to 3 parts sand by volume.

clauses.title: Mortar for Chimney Liners
clauses.text: Chimney liners used in chimneys for oil- or gas-burning appliances shall be laid in a full bed of mortar consisting of 1 part Portland cement to 3 parts sand by volume.

clauses.title: Extension of Chimney Liners
clauses.text: Chimney liners shall extend from a point not less than 200 mm below the lowest flue pipe connection to a point not less than 50 mm or more than 100 mm above the chimney cap.

clauses.title: Unit Masonry
clauses.text: Unit masonry shall conform to Section 9.20.

clauses.title: Concrete
clauses.text: Concrete shall conform to Section 9.3.

clauses.title: Footings
clauses.text: Footings for masonry chimneys and concrete chimneys shall conform to Section 9.15.

clauses.title: Height of Chimney Flues
clauses.text: A chimney flue shall extend not less than a) 900 mm above the highest point at which the chimney comes in contact with the roof, and b) 600 mm above the highest roof surface or structure within 3 m of the chimney. (See Note A-9.21.4.4.(1).)

clauses.title: Lateral Stability
clauses.text: Except as provided in Sentence (2), chimneys shall be braced in accordance with Subsection 4.3.2. to provide lateral stability under wind loads.

clauses.title: Lateral Stability
clauses.text: A chimney need not be laterally braced provided a) no horizontal outside dimension is less than 400 mm, and b) the chimney extends not more than 3.6 m above a roof or the masonry wall of which it forms a part. (See Note A-9.21.4.5.(2).)

clauses.title: Chimney Caps
clauses.text: The top of a chimney shall have a waterproof cap of reinforced concrete, masonry or metal.

clauses.title: Chimney Caps
clauses.text: The cap required in Sentence (1) shall slope from the lining and be provided with a drip not less than 25 mm from the chimney wall.

clauses.title: Chimney Caps
clauses.text: Cast-in-place concrete caps shall be separated from the chimney liner by a bond break and be sealed at that location.

clauses.title: Chimney Caps
clauses.text: Jointed precast concrete or masonry chimney caps shall have flashing installed beneath the cap extending from the liner to the drip edge.

clauses.title: Cleanout
clauses.text: A cleanout opening with a metal frame and a tight-fitting metal door shall be installed near the base of the chimney flue.

clauses.title: Wall Thickness
clauses.text: The walls of a masonry chimney shall be built of solid masonry units not less than 75 mm thick.

clauses.title: Separation of Flue Liners
clauses.text: Flue liners in the same chimney shall be separated by not less than 75 mm of masonry or concrete exclusive of liners where clay liners are used, or 90 mm of firebrick where firebrick liners are used.

clauses.title: Separation of Flue Liners
clauses.text: Flue liners referred to in Sentence (1) shall be installed to prevent significant lateral movement.

clauses.title: Flashing
clauses.text: Junctions with adjacent materials shall be adequately flashed to shed water.

clauses.title: Clearance from Combustible Materials
clauses.text: The clearance between masonry or concrete chimneys and combustible framing shall be not less than a) 50 mm for interior chimneys, and b) 12 mm for exterior chimneys. (See Note A-9.21.5.1.(1).)

clauses.title: Clearance from Combustible Materials
clauses.text: A clearance of not less than 150 mm shall be provided between a cleanout opening and combustible material.

clauses.title: Clearance from Combustible Materials
clauses.text: Combustible flooring and subflooring shall have not less than a 12 mm clearance from masonry or concrete chimneys.

clauses.title: Sealing of Spaces
clauses.text: All spaces between masonry or concrete chimneys and combustible framing shall be sealed top or bottom with noncombustible material.

clauses.title: Support of Joists or Beams
clauses.text: Joists or beams may be supported on masonry walls which enclose chimney flues provided the combustible members are separated from the flue by not less than 290 mm of solid masonry.

clauses.title: Application
clauses.text: Except when otherwise specifically stated herein, this Section applies to masonry fireplaces constructed on-site.

clauses.title: Masonry and Concrete
clauses.text: Except as otherwise stated in this Section, unit masonry shall conform to

clauses.title: Footings
clauses.text: Footings for masonry and concrete fireplaces shall conform to Section 9.15.

clauses.title: Combustion Air
clauses.text: Where a supply of combustion air is provided directly to the fire chamber of a fireplace, including a factory-built fireplace, the installation shall comply with the “Outdoor Air Supply” requirements provided in CAN/CSA-A405-M, “Design and Construction of Masonry Chimneys and Fireplaces.”

clauses.title: Brick or Steel Liners
clauses.text: Except where a fireplace is equipped with a steel liner, every fireplace shall have a firebrick liner.

clauses.title: Firebrick Liners
clauses.text: Firebrick liners shall be not less than a) 50 mm thick for the sides and back, and b) 25 mm thick for the floor.

clauses.title: Firebrick Liners
clauses.text: Firebrick liners shall be laid with high temperature cement mortar conforming to CAN/CGSB-10.3, “Air Setting Refractory Mortar.”

clauses.title: Firebrick Liners
clauses.text: Joints between a firebrick liner and the adjacent backing masonry shall be offset.

clauses.title: Steel Liners
clauses.text: Steel liners for fireplaces shall conform to CAN/ULC-S639, “Standard for Steel Liner Assemblies for Solid-Fuel Burning Masonry Fireplaces,” and shall be installed in accordance with the installation instructions in that standard.

clauses.title: Thickness of Walls
clauses.text: Except as provided in Sentence (2), the thickness of the back and sides of a fireplace, including the thickness of any firebrick liner, shall be not less than 190 mm where a metal liner or a firebrick liner less than 51 mm thick is used.

clauses.title: Thickness of Walls
clauses.text: When a steel fireplace liner is used with an air circulating chamber surrounding the firebox, the back and sides of the fireplace shall consist of a) solid masonry units not less than 90 mm thick, or b) hollow masonry units not less than 190 mm thick.

clauses.title: Fire Chamber Dimensions
clauses.text: The distance from the back of the fire chamber to the plane of the fireplace opening shall be not less than 300 mm.

clauses.title: Hearth Extension
clauses.text: Except as required in Sentence (2), fireplaces shall have a noncombustible hearth extending not less than 400 mm in front of the fireplace opening and not less than 200 mm beyond each side of the fireplace opening.

clauses.title: Hearth Extension
clauses.text: Where the fire chamber floor is elevated more than 150 mm above the hearth, the dimension of the hearth measured perpendicular to the plane of the fireplace opening shall be increased by not less than a) 50 mm for an elevation above 150 mm and not more than 300 mm, and b) an additional 25 mm for every 50 mm in elevation above 300 mm.

clauses.title: Support of Hearth
clauses.text: Except as permitted in Sentence (2), the fire chamber floor and hearth shall be supported on a reinforced concrete slab not less than 100 mm thick at its supports and, if cantilevered, not less than 50 mm thick at its unsupported edge.

clauses.title: Support of Hearth
clauses.text: A hearth for a fireplace with an opening raised not less than 200 mm from a combustible floor is permitted to be supported on that floor provided the requirements of Clauses 5.3.6.5. to 5.3.6.7. of CAN/CSA-A405-M, “Design and Construction of Masonry Chimneys and Fireplaces,” are followed.

clauses.title: Required Damper and Size
clauses.text: The throat of every fireplace shall be equipped with a metal damper sufficiently large to cover the full area of the throat opening.

clauses.title: Slope of Smoke Chamber
clauses.text: The sides of the smoke chamber connecting a fireplace throat with a flue shall not be sloped at an angle greater than 45° to the vertical.

clauses.title: Wall Thickness
clauses.text: The thickness of masonry walls surrounding the smoke chamber shall be not less than 190 mm at the sides, front and back, except that the portions of the back exposed to the outside may be 140 mm thick.

clauses.title: Conformance to Standard
clauses.text: Factory-built fireplaces and their installation shall conform to CAN/ULC-S610, “Standard for Factory-Built Fireplace Systems.”

clauses.title: Clearance to the Fireplace Opening
clauses.text: Combustible material shall not be placed on or near the face of a fireplace within 150 mm of the fireplace opening, except that where the combustible material projects more than 38 mm out from the face of the fireplace above the opening, such material shall be not less than 300 mm above the top of the opening.

clauses.title: Metal Exposed to the Interior
clauses.text: Metal exposed to the interior of a fireplace such as the damper control mechanism shall have not less than a 50 mm clearance from any combustible material on the face of the fireplace where such metal penetrates through the face of the fireplace.

clauses.title: Clearance to Combustible Framing
clauses.text: Not less than a 100 mm clearance shall be provided between the back and sides of a fireplace and combustible framing, except that a 50 mm clearance is permitted where the fireplace is located in an exterior wall.

clauses.title: Clearance to Combustible Framing
clauses.text: Not less than a 50 mm clearance shall be provided between the back and sides of the smoke chamber of a fireplace and combustible framing, except that a 25 mm clearance is permitted where the fireplace is located in an exterior wall.

clauses.title: Heat-Circulating Duct Outlets
clauses.text: The clearance of combustible material above heat-circulating duct outlets from those outlets shall be not less than a) 300 mm where the combustible material projects not less than 38 mm from the face, and b) 150 mm where the projection is less than 38 mm.

clauses.title: Appliance Standard
clauses.text: Fireplace inserts and hearth-mounted stoves vented through the throat of a fireplace shall conform to CAN/ULC 628, “Standard for Fireplace Inserts and Hearth-Mounted Stoves.”

clauses.title: Installation
clauses.text: The installation of fireplace inserts and hearth-mounted stoves vented through the throat of a fireplace shall conform to CSA B365, “Installation Code for Solid-Fuel-Burning Appliances and Equipment.”

clauses.title: Limitations
clauses.text: This Section applies to constructions where wall, floor and roof planes are generally comprised of lumber frames of small repetitive structural members, or engineered components, and where a) roof and wall planes are clad, sheathed or braced on at least one side, b) the small repetitive structural members are spaced not more than 600 mm o.c., c) the constructions do not serve as foundations, d) the specified live load on supported subfloors and floor framing does not exceed 2.4 kPa, and e) the span of any structural member does not exceed 12.20 m. (See Note A-9.23.1.1.(1).)

clauses.title: Limitations
clauses.text: Where the conditions in Sentence (1) are exceeded for wood constructions, the design of the framing and fastening shall conform to Subsection 4.3.1.

clauses.title: Strength and Rigidity
clauses.text: All members shall be so framed, anchored, fastened, tied and braced to provide the necessary strength and rigidity.

clauses.title: Protection from Decay
clauses.text: Ends of wood joists, beams and other members framing into masonry or concrete shall be treated to prevent decay where the bottom of the member is at or below ground level, or a 12 mm air space shall be provided at the end and sides of the member.

clauses.title: Protection from Decay
clauses.text: Air spaces required in Sentence (1) shall not be blocked by insulation, vapour barriers or airtight materials.

clauses.title: Protection from Dampness
clauses.text: Except as permitted in Sentence (2), wood framing members that are not pressure-treated with a wood preservative and that are supported on concrete in contact with the ground or fill shall be separated from the concrete by not less than 0.05 mm polyethylene film or Type S roll roofing.

clauses.title: Protection from Dampness
clauses.text: Dampproofing material referred to in Sentence (1) is not required where the wood member is at least 150 mm above the ground.

clauses.title: Connections to Preservative-Treated Wood
clauses.text: Except as provided in Sentence (3), connectors in contact with preservative-treated wood shall be made of a) hot-dipped, zinc-coated galvanized steel with a coating weight not less than Z550 conforming to ASTM A653/A653M, “Standard Specification for Steel Sheet, Zinc-Coated (Galvanized) or Zinc-Iron Alloy-Coated (Galvannealed) by the Hot-Dip Process,” b) a material that provides an equivalent level of corrosion protection to that provided by the material described in Clause (a), or c) stainless steel.

clauses.title: Connections to Preservative-Treated Wood
clauses.text: Fasteners used to attach the connectors referred to in Sentence (1) shall be made of a) galvanized steel coated with zinc in accordance with ASTM A153/A153M, “Standard Specification for Zinc Coating (Hot-Dip) on Iron and Steel Hardware,” or b) a material that provides an equivalent level of performance and is compatible with the connector.

clauses.title: Connections to Preservative-Treated Wood
clauses.text: Connectors and fasteners that are in contact with wood that has been treated with a disodium octaborate tetrahydrate (SBX (DOT)) or zinc borate preservative and is installed in a dry interior environment are permitted to be made of uncoated carbon steel. (See Note A-9.23.2.4.(3).)

clauses.title: Lumber
clauses.text: Lumber shall conform to Subsection 9.3.2.

clauses.title: Standards for Nails and Screws
clauses.text: Except as provided in Sentence (2) and unless otherwise indicated, nails specified in this Section shall be common steel wire nails or common spiral nails conforming to a) ASTM F1667/F1667M, “Standard Specification for Driven Fasteners: Nails, Spikes, and Staples,” or b) CSA B111, “Wire Nails, Spikes and Staples.”

clauses.title: Length of Nails
clauses.text: All nails shall be long enough so that not less than half their required length penetrates into the second member.

clauses.title: Prevention of Splitting
clauses.text: Splitting of wood members shall be minimized by staggering the nails in the direction of the grain and by keeping nails well in from the edges. (See Note A-9.23.3.3.(1).)

clauses.title: Nailing of Framing
clauses.text: Except as provided in Sentence (2), nailing of framing shall conform to Table 9.23.3.4.

clauses.text: Fastening of sheathing shall conform to Part 4, a) where the 1-in-50 hourly wind pressure is equal to or greater than 1.2 kPa, or b) for required braced wall panels, where the seismic spectral acceleration, Sa(0.2), is greater than 1.8.

clauses.title: Fasteners for Sheathing or Subflooring
clauses.text: Staples shall not be less than 1.6 mm in diameter or thickness, with not less than a 9.5 mm crown driven with the crown parallel to framing.

clauses.title: Fasteners for Sheathing or Subflooring
clauses.text: Roofing nails for the attachment of fibreboard or gypsum sheathing shall not be less than 3.2 mm in diameter with a minimum head diameter of 11.1 mm.

clauses.title: Fasteners for Sheathing or Subflooring
clauses.text: Flooring screws shall not be less than 3.2 mm in diameter.

clauses.title: Fasteners for Sheathing or Subflooring
clauses.text: The edges of sheathing in a braced wall panel shall be supported and fastened to wood blocking where a) the seismic spectral acceleration, Sa(0.2), is greater than 1.2, or b) the braced wall panel supports more than a roof of lightweight construction.

clauses.title: Application
clauses.text: Spans provided in this Subsection for joists, beams and lintels supporting floors shall apply only where a) the floors serve residential areas as described in Table 4.1.5.3., or b) the uniformly distributed live load on the floors does not exceed that specified for residential areas as described in Table 4.1.5.3.

clauses.title: Application
clauses.text: Spans for joists, beams and lintels supporting floors shall be determined according to Subsection 4.1.3. where the supported floors a) serve other than residential areas, or b) support a uniform live load in excess of that specified for residential areas.

clauses.title: Spans for Joists, Rafters and Beams
clauses.text: Except as required in Sentence (2) and Article 9.23.14.10., spans for wood joists and rafters shall conform to the spans shown in Span Tables 9.23.4.2.-A to 9.23.4.2.-G for the uniform live loads shown in the Tables. (See Article 9.4.2.2.)

clauses.title: Spans for Joists, Rafters and Beams
clauses.text: Spans for floor joists that are not selected from Span Tables 9.23.4.2.-A and 9.23.4.2.-B and that are required to be designed for the same loading conditions, shall not exceed the design requirements for uniform loading and vibration criteria. (See Note A-9.23.4.2.(2).)

clauses.title: Spans for Joists, Rafters and Beams
clauses.text: Spans for built-up wood and glued-laminated timber floor beams shall conform to the spans in Span Tables 9.23.4.2.-H to 9.23.4.2.-K. (See Article 9.4.2.2.)

clauses.title: Spans for Joists, Rafters and Beams
clauses.text: Spans for roof ridge beams shall conform to the spans in Span Table 9.23.4.2.-L for the uniform snow load shown. (See Articles 9.4.2.2. and 9.23.14.8.)

clauses.title: Steel Beams
clauses.text: The spans for steel floor beams with laterally supported top flanges shall conform to Table 9.23.4.3. (See Note A-9.23.4.3.(1).)

clauses.title: Concrete Topping
clauses.text: Except as permitted in Sentence (2), where a floor is required to support a concrete topping, the joist spans shown in Span Table 9.23.4.2.-A or the spacing of the members shall be reduced to allow for the loads due to the topping.

clauses.title: Concrete Topping
clauses.text: Where a floor is required to support a concrete topping, joist spans are permitted to be selected from Span Table 9.23.4.2.-B provided the concrete a) is 38 to 51 mm thick, b) is normal weight, c) is placed directly on the subflooring, and d) has not less than 20 MPa compressive strength after 28 days.

clauses.title: Concrete Topping
clauses.text: Where a floor is required to support a concrete topping not more than 51 mm thick, the allowable beam spans shown in Span Tables 9.23.4.2.-H to 9.23.4.2.-K shall be multiplied by 0.8 or the supported length of the floor joists shall be reduced to allow for the loads due to the topping.

clauses.title: Heavy Roofing Materials
clauses.text: Where a roof is required to support an additional uniform dead load from roofing materials such as concrete roofing tile, or materials other than as specified in Section 9.26., such as clay roofing tiles, the additional load shall be allowed for by reducing a) the spans for roof joists and rafters in Span Tables 9.23.4.2.-D to 9.23.4.2.-G, or the spacing of the members, and b) the spans for ridge beams and lintels in Span Tables 9.23.4.2.-L and 9.23.12.3.-A to 9.23.12.3.-D. (See Note A-9.23.4.2.)

clauses.title: Holes Drilled in Framing Members
clauses.text: Holes drilled in roof, floor or ceiling framing members shall be not larger than one-quarter the depth of the member and shall be located not less than 50 mm from the edges, unless the depth of the member is increased by the size of the hole.

clauses.title: Notching of Framing Members
clauses.text: Floor, roof and ceiling framing members are permitted to be notched provided the notch is located on the top of the member within half the joist depth from the edge of bearing and is not deeper than one-third the joist depth, unless the depth of the member is increased by the size of the notch.

clauses.title: Wall Studs
clauses.text: Wall studs shall not be notched, drilled or otherwise damaged so that the undamaged portion of the stud is less than two-thirds the depth of the stud if the stud is loadbearing or 40 mm if the stud is non-loadbearing, unless the weakened studs are suitably reinforced.

clauses.title: Top Plates
clauses.text: Top plates in walls shall not be notched, drilled or otherwise weakened to reduce the undamaged width to less than 50 mm unless the weakened plates are suitably reinforced.

clauses.title: Roof Trusses
clauses.text: Roof truss members shall not be notched, drilled or otherwise weakened unless such notching or drilling is allowed for in the design of the truss.

clauses.title: Anchorage of Building Frames
clauses.text: Except as required by Sentence 9.23.6.3.(1), building frames shall be anchored to the foundation unless a structural analysis that considers wind and earthquake loads and lateral earth pressures shows that anchorage is not required.

clauses.title: Anchorage of Building Frames
clauses.text: Except as provided in Sentences (3) to (6), anchorage shall be provided by a) embedding the ends of the first floor joists in concrete, b) fastening the sill plate to the foundation with not less than 12.7 mm diam anchor bolts spaced not more than 2.4 m o.c., or c) embedding in concrete two 38 mm by 89 mm sill plates, placed on edge and separated by blocking spaced 1.2 m o.c.

tables.title: Anchor Bolt Spacing where the 1-in-50 HWP ≤ 1.20 kPa and 0.70 < Sa(0.2) ≤ 1.8

clauses.title: Anchorage of Building Frames
clauses.text: For buildings with 2 or more floors supported by frame walls that are in areas where the seismic spectral acceleration, Sa(0.2), is not greater than 0.70 or the 1-in-50 hourly wind pressure (HWP) is equal to or greater than 0.80 kPa but not greater than 1.20 kPa, anchorage shall be provided by fastening the sill plate to the foundation with not less than two anchor bolts per braced wall panel, where all anchor bolts used are a) not less than 15.9 mm in diameter, located within 0.5 m of the end of the foundation, and spaced not more than 2.4 m o.c, or b) not less than 12.7 mm in diameter, located within 0.5 m of the end of the foundation, and spaced not more than 1.7 m o.c.

clauses.title: Anchorage of Building Frames
clauses.text: Anchor bolts referred to in Sentences (2) to (4) shall be a) fastened to the sill plate with nuts and washers, b) embedded not less than 100 mm in the foundation, and c) so designed that they may be tightened without withdrawing them from the foundation.

clauses.title: Anchorage of Building Frames
clauses.text: Where the seismic spectral acceleration, Sa(0.2), is greater than 1.8 or the 1-in-50 hourly wind pressure is equal to or greater than 1.2 kPa, anchorage shall be designed according to Part 4.

clauses.title: Anchorage of Columns and Posts
clauses.text: Except as provided in Sentences (2) and (3), exterior columns and posts shall be anchored to resist uplift and lateral movement.

clauses.title: Anchorage of Columns and Posts
clauses.text: Except as provided in Sentence (3), where columns or posts support balconies, decks, verandas or other exterior platforms, and the distance from finished ground to the underside of the joists is not more than 600 mm, a) the columns or posts shall be anchored to the foundation to resist uplift and lateral movement, or b) the supported joists or beams shall be directly anchored to the ground to resist uplift.

clauses.title: Anchorage of Columns and Posts
clauses.text: Anchorage is not required for platforms described in Sentence (2) that a) are not more than 1 storey in height, b) are not more than 55 m2 in area, c) do not support a roof, and d) are not attached to another structure, unless it can be demonstrated that differential movement will not adversely affect the performance of the structure to which the platform is attached.

clauses.title: Anchorage of Smaller Buildings
clauses.text: Buildings not more than 4.3 m wide and not more than 1 storey in building height that are not anchored in accordance with Sentence 9.23.6.1.(1) shall be anchored in conformance with the requirements of CSA Z240.10.1, “Site preparation, foundation, and installation of buildings.”

clauses.title: Size of Sill Plates
clauses.text: Where sill plates provide bearing for the floor system, they shall be not less than 38 mm by 89 mm material.

clauses.title: Levelling and Sealing of Sill Plates
clauses.text: Sill plates shall be a) levelled by setting them on a full bed of mortar, or b) laid directly on the foundation if the top of the foundation is level. (See also Article 9.23.2.3.)

clauses.title: Levelling and Sealing of Sill Plates
clauses.text: The joint between the sill plate for exterior walls and the foundation shall be sealed in accordance with Subsection 9.25.3.

clauses.title: Bearing for Beams
clauses.text: Beams shall have even and level bearing and the bearing at end supports shall be not less than 89 mm long, except as stated in the notes to Span Tables 9.23.4.2.-H to 9.23.4.2.-K.

clauses.title: Priming of Steel Beams
clauses.text: Exterior steel beams shall be shop primed.

clauses.title: Built-up Wood Beams
clauses.text: Where a beam is made up of individual pieces of lumber that are nailed together, the individual members shall be 38 mm or greater in thickness and installed on edge.

clauses.title: Built-up Wood Beams
clauses.text: Except as permitted in Sentence (3), where individual members of a built-up beam are butted together to form a joint, the joint shall occur over a support.

clauses.title: Built-up Wood Beams
clauses.text: Where a beam is continuous over more than one span, individual members are permitted to be butted together to form a joint at or within 150 mm of the end quarter points of the clear spans, provided the quarter points are not those closest to the ends of the beam.

clauses.title: Built-up Wood Beams
clauses.text: Members joined at quarter points shall be continuous over adjacent supports.

clauses.title: Built-up Wood Beams
clauses.text: Joints in individual members of a beam that are located at or near the end quarter points shall not occur in adjacent members at the same quarter point and shall not reduce the effective beam width by more than half.

clauses.title: Built-up Wood Beams
clauses.text: Not more than one butt joint shall occur in any individual member of a built-up beam within any one span.

clauses.title: Built-up Wood Beams
clauses.text: Except as provided in Sentence (8), where 38 mm members are laid on edge to form a built-up beam, individual members shall be nailed together with a double row of nails not less than 89 mm in length, spaced not more than 450 mm apart in each row with the end nails located 100 mm to 150 mm from the end of each piece.

clauses.title: Built-up Wood Beams
clauses.text: Where 38 mm members in built-up wood beams are not nailed together as provided in Sentence (7), they shall be bolted together with not less than 12.7 mm diam bolts equipped with washers and spaced not more than 1.2 m o.c., with the end bolts located not more than 600 mm from the ends of the members.

clauses.title: End Bearing for Joists
clauses.text: Except when supported on ribbon boards, floor joists shall have not less than 38 mm length of end bearing.

clauses.title: End Bearing for Joists
clauses.text: Ribbon boards referred to in Sentence (1) shall be not less than 19 mm by 89 mm lumber let into the studs.

clauses.title: Joists Supported by Beams
clauses.text: Floor joists may be supported on the tops of beams or may be framed into the sides of beams.

clauses.title: Joists Supported by Beams
clauses.text: When framed into the side of a wood beam, joists referred to in Sentence (1) shall be supported on a) joist hangers or other acceptable mechanical connectors, or b) not less than 38 mm by 64 mm ledger strips nailed to the side of the beam, except that 38 mm by 38 mm ledger strips may be used provided each joist is nailed to the beam by not less than four 89 mm nails, in addition to the nailing for the ledger strip required in Table 9.23.3.4.

clauses.title: Joists Supported by Beams
clauses.text: When framed into the side of a steel beam, joists referred to in Sentence (1) shall be supported on the bottom flange of the beam or on not less than 38 mm by 38 mm lumber bolted to the web with not less than 6.3 mm diam bolts spaced not more than 600 mm apart.

clauses.title: Joists Supported by Beams
clauses.text: Joists referred to in Sentence (3) shall be spliced above the beam with not less than 38 mm by 38 mm lumber at least 600 mm long to support the flooring.

clauses.title: Joists Supported by Beams
clauses.text: Not less than a 12 mm space shall be provided between the splice required in Sentence (4) and the beam to allow for shrinkage of the wood joists.

clauses.title: Restraint of Joist Bottoms
clauses.text: Except as provided in Sentence 9.23.9.4.(1), bottoms of floor joists shall be restrained from twisting at each end by toe-nailing to the supports, end-nailing to the header joists or by providing continuous strapping, blocking between the joists or cross-bridging near the supports.

clauses.title: Strapping, Bridging, Furring and Ceilings in Span Tables 9.23.4.2.-A
clauses.text: Except as permitted by Sentence (5), where strapping is specified in Span Table 9.23.4.2.-A, it shall be a) not less than 19 mm by 64 mm, nailed to the underside of floor joists, b) located not more than 2 100 mm from each support or other rows of strapping, and c) fastened at each end to a sill or header.

clauses.title: Strapping, Bridging, Furring and Ceilings in Span Tables 9.23.4.2.-A
clauses.text: Where bridging is specified in Span Table 9.23.4.2.-A, it shall consist of not less than 19 mm by 64 mm or 38 mm by 38 mm cross bridging located not more than 2 100 mm from each support or other rows of bridging.

clauses.title: Strapping, Bridging, Furring and Ceilings in Span Tables 9.23.4.2.-A
clauses.text: Where bridging and strapping are specified in Span Table 9.23.4.2.-A, a) bridging shall i) comply with Sentence (2), or ii) consist of 38 mm solid blocking located not more than 2 100 mm from each support or other rows of bridging and securely fastened between the joists, and b) except as provided in Sentence (5), strapping shall comply with Sentence (1) and be installed under the bridging.

clauses.title: Strapping, Bridging, Furring and Ceilings in Span Tables 9.23.4.2.-A
clauses.text: Bridging specified in Span Table 9.23.4.2.-B shall consist of a) bridging as described in Sentence (2), or b) 38 mm solid blocking located not more than 2 100 mm from each support or other rows of bridging and securely fastened between the joists.

clauses.title: Strapping, Bridging, Furring and Ceilings in Span Tables 9.23.4.2.-A
clauses.text: Strapping described in Sentence (1) and Clause (3)(b) is not required where a) furring strips complying with Table 9.29.3.1. are fastened directly to the joists, or b) a panel-type ceiling finish complying with Subsection 9.29.5., 9.29.6., 9.29.7., 9.29.8., or 9.29.9. is attached directly to the joists.

clauses.title: Strapping, Bridging, Furring and Ceilings in Span Tables 9.23.4.2.-A
clauses.text: Where a ceiling attached to wood furring is specified in Span Table 9.23.4.2.-B, a) the ceiling finish shall consist of gypsum board, plywood or OSB not less than 12.7 mm thick, and b) the furring shall be i) 19 mm by 89 mm wood furring spaced at not more than 600 mm o.c., or ii) 19 mm by 64 mm wood furring spaced at not more than 400 mm o.c.

clauses.title: Header Joists
clauses.text: Header joists around floor openings shall be doubled when they exceed 1.2 m in length.

clauses.title: Header Joists
clauses.text: The size of header joists exceeding 3.2 m in length shall be determined by calculations.

clauses.title: Trimmer Joists
clauses.text: Trimmer joists around floor openings shall be doubled when the length of the header joist exceeds 800 mm.

clauses.title: Trimmer Joists
clauses.text: When the header joist exceeds 2 m in length the size of the trimmer joists shall be determined by calculations.

clauses.title: Support of Tail and Header Joists
clauses.text: When tail joists and header joists are supported by the floor framing, they shall be supported by suitable joist hangers or nailing in accordance with Table 9.23.3.4.

clauses.title: Support of Walls
clauses.text: Non-loadbearing walls parallel to the floor joists shall be supported by joists beneath the wall or on blocking between the joists.

clauses.title: Support of Walls
clauses.text: Blocking referred to in Sentence (1) for the support of non-loadbearing walls shall be a) not less than 38 mm by 89 mm lumber, and b) except as required for the fastening of walls constructed with required braced wall panels, spaced not more than 1.2 m apart.

clauses.title: Support of Walls
clauses.text: Except as provided in Sentence (6), non-loadbearing interior walls at right angles to the floor joists are not restricted as to location.

clauses.title: Support of Walls
clauses.text: Loadbearing interior walls parallel to floor joists shall be supported by beams or walls of sufficient strength to safely transfer the specified live loads to the vertical supports.

clauses.title: Support of Walls
clauses.text: Unless the joist size is designed to support such loads, loadbearing interior walls at right angles to floor joists shall be located a) not more than 900 mm from the joist support where the wall does not support a floor, and b) not more than 600 mm from the joist support where the wall supports one or more floors.

clauses.title: Support of Walls
clauses.text: Loadbearing and non-loadbearing walls constructed with required braced wall panels shall be continuously supported by floor joists, blocking or rim joists to allow for the required fastening (see Table 9.23.3.4.).

clauses.title: Cantilevered Floor Joists
clauses.text: Floor joists supporting roof loads shall not be cantilevered more than 400 mm beyond their supports where 38 mm by 184 mm joists are used and not more than 600 mm beyond their supports where 38 mm by 235 mm or larger joists are used.

clauses.title: Cantilevered Floor Joists
clauses.text: The cantilevered portions referred to in Sentence (1) shall not support floor loads from other storeys unless calculations are provided to show that the design resistances of the cantilevered joists are not exceeded.

clauses.title: Cantilevered Floor Joists
clauses.text: Where cantilevered floor joists described in Sentences (1) and (2) are at right angles to the main floor joists, the tail joists in the cantilevered portion shall extend inward away from the cantilever support a distance equal to not less than 6 times the length of the cantilever, and shall be end nailed to an interior doubled header joist in conformance with Table 9.23.3.4.

clauses.title: Stud Size and Spacing
clauses.text: The size and spacing of studs shall conform to Table 9.23.10.1. Table 9.23.10.1. clauses.title: Bracing and Lateral Support
clauses.text: Where loadbearing interior walls are not finished in accordance with Section 9.29., blocking or strapping shall be fastened to the studs at mid-height to prevent sideways buckling.

clauses.title: Orientation of Studs
clauses.text: Except as permitted in Sentences (2) and (3), all studs shall be placed at right angles to the wall face.

clauses.title: Orientation of Studs
clauses.text: Studs on the flat are permitted to be used in gable ends of roofs that contain only unfinished space or in non-loadbearing interior walls within the limits described in Article 9.23.10.1.

clauses.title: Orientation of Studs
clauses.text: Wall studs that support only a load from an attic not accessible by a stairway are permitted to be placed on the flat within the limits permitted in Article 9.23.10.1. provided a) the studs are clad on not less than one side with plywood, OSB or waferboard sheathing fastened to the face of the studs with a structural adhesive, and b) the portion of the roof supported by the studs does not exceed 2.1 m in width.

clauses.title: Continuity of Studs
clauses.text: Wall studs shall be continuous for the full storey height except at openings and shall not be spliced except by fingerjoining with a structural adhesive. (See Note A-9.23.10.4.(1).)

clauses.title: Support for Cladding, Sheathing and Finishing Materials
clauses.text: Corners and intersections shall be designed to provide adequate support for the vertical edges of interior finishes, sheathing and cladding materials, and in no instance shall exterior corners be framed with less than the equivalent of 2 studs.

clauses.title: Support for Cladding, Sheathing and Finishing Materials
clauses.text: Where the vertical edges of interior finishes at wall intersections are supported at vertical intervals by blocking or furring, the vertical distance between such supports shall not exceed the maximum distance between supports specified in Section 9.29.

clauses.title: Studs at Sides of Openings
clauses.text: Where the lintel spanning the opening is more than 3 m long, studs shall be tripled on each side of the opening so that a) the two inner studs on each side extend from the bottom of the supported lintel to the top of the bottom wall plate, and b) the outer stud on each side extends from the bottom of the top wall plate to the bottom wall plate.

clauses.title: Studs at Sides of Openings
clauses.text: Except as provided in Sentence (3), where the lintel spanning the opening is not more than 3 m long, studs shall be doubled on each side of the opening so that a) the inner studs on each side extend from the bottom of the supported lintel to the top of the bottom wall plate, and b) the outer stud on each side extends from the bottom of the top wall plate to the bottom wall plate.

clauses.title: Studs at Sides of Openings
clauses.text: Single studs are permitted to be used on either side of openings a) in non-loadbearing interior walls not required to have fire-resistance ratings, provided the studs extend from the top wall plate to the bottom wall plate, or b) in loadbearing or non-loadbearing interior or exterior walls, provided i) the opening is less than and within the required stud spacing, and ii) no 2 such openings of full stud-space width are located in adjacent stud spaces. (See Note A-9.23.10.6.(3).)

clauses.title: Size of Wall Plates
clauses.text: Except as provided in Sentence (2), wall plates shall be a) not less than 38 mm thick, and b) not less than the required width of the wall studs.

clauses.title: Size of Wall Plates
clauses.text: In non-loadbearing walls and in loadbearing walls where the studs are located directly over framing members, the bottom wall plate is permitted to be 19 mm thick.

clauses.title: Bottom Wall Plates
clauses.text: A bottom wall plate shall be provided in all cases.

clauses.title: Bottom Wall Plates
clauses.text: The bottom plate in exterior walls shall not project more than one-third the plate width over the support.

clauses.title: Top Plates
clauses.text: Except as permitted in Sentences (2) to (4), at least 2 top plates shall be provided in loadbearing walls.

clauses.title: Top Plates
clauses.text: A single top plate is permitted to be used in a section of a loadbearing wall containing a lintel provided the top plate forms a tie across the lintel.

clauses.title: Top Plates
clauses.text: A single top plate is permitted to be used in loadbearing walls where the concentrated loads from ceilings, floors and roofs are not more than 50 mm to one side of the supporting studs and in all non-loadbearing walls.

clauses.title: Top Plates
clauses.text: The top plates need not be provided in a section of loadbearing wall containing a lintel provided the lintel is tied to the adjacent wall section with not less than a) 75 mm by 150 mm by 0.91 mm thick galvanized steel, or b) 19 mm by 89 mm by 300 mm wood splice nailed to each wall section with at least three 63 mm nails.

clauses.title: Joints in Top Plates
clauses.text: Joints in the top plates of loadbearing walls shall be staggered not less than one stud spacing.

clauses.title: Joints in Top Plates
clauses.text: The top plates in loadbearing walls shall be lapped or otherwise tied at corners and intersecting walls in accordance with Sentence (4).

clauses.title: Joints in Top Plates
clauses.text: Joints in single top plates used with loadbearing walls shall be tied in accordance with Sentence (4).

clauses.text: Ties referred to in Sentences (2) and (3) shall be the equivalent of not less than 75 mm by 150 mm by 0.91 mm thick galvanized steel nailed to each wall with at least three 63 mm nails.

clauses.text: Where the seismic spectral acceleration, Sa(0.2), is greater than 0.70 but not more than 1.8, doubled top plates in braced wall bands shall be fastened on each side of a splice with 76 mm long common steel wire nails or spiral nails in accordance with Table 9.23.11.4. clauses.title: Openings in Non-Loadbearing Walls
clauses.text: Except as provided in Sentence (2), openings in non-loadbearing walls shall be framed with not less than 38 mm material the same width as the studs, securely nailed to adjacent studs.

clauses.title: Openings in Non-Loadbearing Walls
clauses.text: Openings for doors in non-loadbearing walls required to be fire separations with a fire-resistance rating shall be framed with the equivalent of at least two 38 mm thick members that are the same width as the wall plates.

clauses.title: Openings in Loadbearing Walls
clauses.text: Openings in loadbearing walls greater than the required stud spacing shall be framed with lintels designed to carry the superimposed loads to adjacent studs. (See Note A-9.23.10.6.(3).)

clauses.title: Openings in Loadbearing Walls
clauses.text: Except as provided in Sentence 9.23.12.3.(2), where 2 or more members are used in lintels, they shall be fastened together with not less than 82 mm nails in a double row, with nails not more than 450 mm apart in each row.

clauses.title: Openings in Loadbearing Walls
clauses.text: Lintel members are permitted to be separated by filler pieces.

clauses.title: Lintel Spans and Sizes
clauses.text: Spans and sizes of wood lintels shall conform to the spans shown in Span Tables 9.23.4.2.-L and 9.23.12.3.-A to 9.23.12.3.-D a) for buildings of residential occupancy, b) where the wall studs exceed 38 mm by 64 mm in size, c) where the spans of supported joists do not exceed 4.9 m, and d) where the spans of trusses do not exceed 9.8 m.

clauses.title: Lintel Spans and Sizes
clauses.text: In loadbearing exterior and interior walls of 38 mm by 64 mm framing members, lintels shall consist of a) 64 mm thick members on edge, or b) 38 mm thick and 19 mm thick members fastened together with a double row of nails not less than 63 mm long and spaced not more than 450 mm apart.

clauses.title: Lintel Spans and Sizes
clauses.text: Lintels referred to in Sentence (2) a) shall be not less than 50 mm greater in depth than those shown in Span Tables 9.23.4.2.-L and 9.23.12.3.-A to 9.23.12.3.-D for the maximum spans shown, and b) shall not exceed 2.24 m in length.

clauses.title: Requirements for Low to Moderate Wind and Seismic Forces
clauses.text: This Article applies in locations where the seismic spectral acceleration, Sa(0.2), is not more than 0.70 and the 1-in-50 hourly wind pressure is less than 0.80 kPa.

clauses.title: Requirements for Low to Moderate Wind and Seismic Forces
clauses.text: Bracing to resist lateral loads shall be designed and constructed as follows: a) exterior walls shall be i) clad with panel-type cladding in accordance with Section 9.27., ii) sheathed with plywood, OSB, waferboard, fibreboard, gypsum board or diagonal lumber sheathing complying with Subsection 9.23.17. and fastened in accordance with Table 9.23.3.5.-A, or iii) finished on the interior with a panel-type material in accordance with the requirements of Section 9.29., or b) in accordance with i) Articles 9.23.13.4. to 9.23.13.7., ii) Part 4, or iii) good engineering practice such as that provided in CWC 2014, “Engineering Guide for Wood Frame Construction.”

clauses.title: Requirements for High Wind and Seismic Forces
clauses.text: Except as provided in Article 9.23.13.1., this Article applies in locations where a) the seismic spectral acceleration, Sa(0.2), is greater than 0.70 but not more than 1.8 and i) the lowest exterior frame wall supports not more than 1 floor in buildings of heavy construction (see Note A-9.23.13.2.(1)(a)(i)), or ii) the lowest exterior frame wall supports not more than 2 floors in other types of construction, and b) the 1-in-50 hourly wind pressure is less than 1.20 kPa.

clauses.title: Requirements for High Wind and Seismic Forces
clauses.text: Bracing to resist lateral loads shall be designed and constructed in accordance with a) Articles 9.23.13.4. to 9.23.13.7., b) Part 4, or c) good engineering practice such as that provided in CWC 2014, “Engineering Guide for Wood Frame Construction.”

clauses.title: Requirements for Extreme Wind and Seismic Forces
clauses.text: Except as provided in Articles 9.23.13.1. and 9.23.13.2., this Article applies in locations where a) the seismic spectral acceleration, Sa(0.2), is i) greater than 1.8, ii) greater than 0.70 and the lowest exterior frame wall supports more than 2 floors in buildings of light construction, or iii) greater than 0.70 and the lowest exterior frame wall supports more than 1 floor in buildings of heavy construction, or b) the 1-in-50 hourly wind pressure is equal to or greater than 1.20 kPa.

clauses.title: Requirements for Extreme Wind and Seismic Forces
clauses.text: Bracing to resist lateral loads shall be designed and constructed in accordance with a) Part 4, or b) good engineering practice such as that provided in CWC 2014, “Engineering Guide for Wood Frame Construction.”

clauses.title: Braced Wall Bands
clauses.text: Braced wall bands shall a) be full storey height, b) be not more than 1.2 m wide, c) lap at both ends with another braced wall band, d) be aligned with braced wall bands on storeys above and below, and e) conform to the spacing and dimensions given in Table 9.23.13.5.

clauses.text: For split-level buildings, a braced wall band shall be located where there is a change in floor level greater than the depth of one floor joist.

clauses.text: Except as provided in Sentences (2) to (5) and Article 9.23.13.7., braced wall panels shall a) be located within braced wall bands, b) extend, as applicable, from the top of the supporting footing, slab or subfloor to the underside of the floor, ceiling or roof framing above, and c) conform to the spacing and dimensions given in Table 9.23.13.5. clauses.title: Braced Wall Panels in Braced Wall Bands
clauses.text: In basements or crawl spaces where the perimeter foundation walls extend from the footings to the underside of the supported floor, braced wall bands constructed with braced wall panels shall be spaced not more than a) 15 m from the perimeter foundation walls, b) 15 m from interior foundation walls, and c) 15 m from adjacent braced wall bands constructed with braced wall panels. (See Note A-9.23.13.5.(2).)

clauses.title: Braced Wall Panels in Braced Wall Bands
clauses.text: Portions of the perimeter of a single open or enclosed space need not comply with Sentence (1), where a) the roof of the space projects not more than i) 3.5 m from the face of the framing of the nearest parallel braced wall band, and ii) the perpendicular plan dimension, b) that portion of the perimeter structure does not support a floor, c) the roof of the space is i) integral with the roof of the rest of the building with framing members not more than 400 mm o.c. where roof sheathing edges are not supported on blocking and not more than 600 mm o.c. where roof sheathing edges are supported on blocking securely fastened between framing members, or ii) constructed with roof framing not more than 400 mm o.c. where roof sheathing edges are not supported on blocking and not more than 600 mm o.c. where roof sheathing edges are supported on blocking securely fastened between framing members, and fastened to the wall framing (see Table 9.23.3.4. and Article 9.23.9.1. for balloon framing), and d) the end-joists or end-rafters for the roof of the space are fastened to a 3-ply, 38 mm × 140 mm built-up column or a 5-ply, 38 mm × 89 mm built-up column that is integral with the wall framing. (See Note A-9.23.13.5.(3).)

clauses.title: Braced Wall Panels in Braced Wall Bands
clauses.text: Walls in detached garages and in accessory buildings serving a single dwelling unit, and the front wall of attached garages serving a single dwelling unit need not comply with Sentence (1) where these walls do not support a floor.

clauses.title: Braced Wall Panels in Braced Wall Bands
clauses.text: Braced wall panels in the braced wall band at the front of an attached garage serving a single dwelling unit need not comply with Sentence (1), provided a) the maximum spacing between the front of the garage and the back wall of the garage does not exceed 7.6 m, b) there is not more than one floor above the garage, c) not less than 50% of the length of the back wall of the garage is constructed of braced wall panels, and d) not less than 25% of the length of the side walls is constructed of braced wall panels.

clauses.title: Materials in Braced Wall Panels
clauses.text: Required braced wall panels shall be a) clad with panel-type cladding complying with Section 9.27. and Table 9.23.3.4., b) sheathed with plywood, OSB, waferboard or diagonal lumber sheathing complying with Subsection 9.23.16. and Table 9.23.13.6., and fastened in accordance with Article 9.23.3.5., or c) finished on the interior with a panel-type material in accordance with the requirements of Section 9.29. and Table 9.23.13.6.
